a_rows_sample.anchor: Vocabulary -> Relations -> State -> Transitions -> InvariantPreservation. The next step should therefore be not another philosophical layer. It is time to derive the actual DDD structures.
a_rows_sample.statement: Names the architecture's maturity progression (Concepts->Relations->StateSpaces->Transitions->InvariantPreservation) as complete, and declares readiness to move from theory-building to deriving actual DDD structures.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Which objects must change atomically, and therefore belong to the same Aggregate? ... Atomicity+InvariantOwnership+TransactionBoundary+Identity+Lifecycle+Concurrency. ... Vocabulary -> Relations -> State -> Transitions -> Invariants -> Aggregates -> BoundedContexts.
a_rows_sample.statement: Opens Step 205: derive candidate Aggregate boundaries using Atomicity, InvariantOwnership, TransactionBoundary, Identity, Lifecycle, and Concurrency, testing each candidate against 'why does this object own this invariant?' and 'what must be immediately vs eventually consistent?'; explicitly names and mandates preserving the full seven-stage derivation order (Vocabulary->Relations->State->Transitions->Invariants->Aggregates->BoundedContexts) in the book itself, to demonstrate how the architecture was actually derived rather than presenting a finished design as if it had been upfront.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DDD-2 | Aggregate adjudication (189's five vs 205's lists): apply 203 section34's own criterion (Same Aggregate iff shared transactional invariant requires atomicity) to the KI catalogue per candidate
a_rows_sample.statement: DDD-2 adjudicates between step 189's five candidate aggregates and step 205's aggregate lists by applying step 203 section 34's own same-aggregate criterion (Same Aggregate if and only if a shared transactional invariant requires atomicity) to the KI catalogue per candidate; produces a per-candidate verdict showing the criterion's evaluation explicitly, resolving Lineage and Determination disagreements by the criterion or marking them UNRESOLVED.

b_rows_sample.anchor: UbiquitousLanguage+SemanticModel+InvariantOwnership+Team/Responsibility+Lifecycle+ChangeRate+IntegrationNeed and especially: Where does the meaning of a word change? That question is the true DDD boundary detector.
b_rows_sample.statement: Opens Step 206 (outside this batch): finally deriving the Bounded Context Map, testing each candidate boundary against seven criteria and especially the question 'where does the meaning of a word change?', explicitly the true DDD boundary detector -- reframing the question from 'how many microservices?' to 'where does KnowledgeOS need a different model of reality?'

b_rows_sample.anchor: 206.1 Aggregate != Bounded Context. Aggregate = ConsistencyBoundary, whereas BoundedContext = ModelBoundary. Therefore a bounded context can contain several aggregates: BC_i={Agg_1,Agg_2,...,Agg_n}. ... 206.2 The central DDD question. For every important term x, ask Meaning(x|BC_i) and compare with Meaning(x|BC_j). If they differ, we have evidence for a bounded-context boundary.
b_rows_sample.statement: Opens Step 206 by distinguishing Aggregate (a ConsistencyBoundary) from BoundedContext (a ModelBoundary), noting one bounded context can contain several aggregates; states the central DDD boundary test: for any important term x, compare Meaning(x|BC_i) against Meaning(x|BC_j) -- a difference is evidence for a genuine context boundary, judged much stronger than merely observing 'these belong to different modules'. Illustrates with the term 'Decision', which means an assessed conclusion in an epistemic context, an authorized organizational determination in a governance context, and an instruction to execute in an operational context, boxing Decision_Epistemic != Decision_Governance != Decision_Operational, and recommending distinct concepts (EpistemicConclusion, GovernanceDecision, ExecutionCommand) connected by explicit relationships rather than one universal Decision object -- while explicitly not yet freezing these exact names.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 206.5 Candidate context: Evidence ... 206.6 Candidate context: Epistemic Assessment ... 206.7 Candidate context: Model ... 206.8 Candidate context: Governance ... IsTrue != IsPermitted
b_rows_sample.statement: Derives four candidate bounded contexts from semantic divergence: Evidence Context, whose central concern is what information can be treated as evidence with what provenance/integrity/source/version/validity, not what should be done; Assessment Context, formalized as A=f(P,E,M,C) -- concluding what can currently be concluded given evidence and model, distinct from merely storing evidence; Model/Method context, since a statistical or AI model version has its own lifecycle (trained/evaluated/validated/approved/retired) that Assessment merely consumes (Assessment -uses-> ModelVersion) without owning; and Governance Context, whose vocabulary (Policy, Authority, Approval, Mandate, Constraint) answers what is permitted/authorized/required/prohibited, fundamentally different from Evidence/Assessment's concern with what is true -- boxed as IsTrue != IsPermitted, called a foundational distinction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 206.9 Candidate context: Decision ... Policy != Decision. A Governance context could contain both, or Decision could become a separate context ... We should not split them prematurely. ... 206.10 Candidate context: Execution ... Authorization != Execution. This is one of our strongest context boundaries. ... 206.11 Candidate context: Observation
b_rows_sample.statement: Derives three further candidate contexts: Decision, distinguished from GovernancePolicy (a policy P(x) establishes rules, a decision D(x,C) applies them to a concrete situation, giving Policy != Decision) but explicitly not split from Governance prematurely pending evidence of an independently evolving model; Execution, whose vocabulary (Command, Job, Run, Status, Failure, Retry, Completion) concerns how an authorized action is made to happen rather than whether it should happen, boxed as Authorization != Execution and called one of the strongest context boundaries derived; and Observation, concerning ObservedEvent/Measurement/Outcome/Deviation/Feedback, which feeds back into Evidence (OutcomeObservation -> Evidence), making the overall organizational architecture cyclic (Knowledge -> Decision -> Action -> Outcome -> Knowledge), explicitly framed as learning rather than a defect.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 206.12 The KnowledgeOS loop ... Observe -> Evidence -> Assess -> Govern -> Decide -> Act -> Observe ... 206.13 Why feedback matters mathematically ... K_{t+1} = U(K_t, H(F(X_t,A_t,epsilon_t),eta_t)). ... 206.14 But KnowledgeOS is not merely a control system
b_rows_sample.statement: Assembles the seven candidate contexts into a single cyclic loop Observe -> Evidence -> Assess -> Govern -> Decide -> Act -> Observe, described as the most compact representation derived so far but explicitly warned not to be read as a linear workflow -- it is a feedback system. Formalizes this mathematically: given knowledge state K_t, action A_t changes the environment via X_{t+1}=F(X_t,A_t,epsilon_t), observation O_{t+1}=H(X_{t+1},eta_t) updates knowledge via K_{t+1}=U(K_t,O_{t+1}), combining into the boxed equation K_{t+1}=U(K_t,H(F(X_t,A_t,epsilon_t),eta_t)) -- a genuine feedback-control structure. Immediately qualifies this: KnowledgeOS is not merely a control system, since it additionally contains meaning, governance, evidence, human judgment, authority, uncertainty, and organizational memory that a pure target-control-correction model does not capture -- the control-theoretic model is explicitly demoted to a lens, not the complete architecture.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 206.16 We need another DDD test ... boundary score: B(i,j) = w_L*D_L + w_I*D_I + w_C*D_C + w_O*D_O + w_T*D_T. ... 206.17 Semantic distance d_sem(BC_i,BC_j). ... 206.18 But beware of false precision ... The formula is a reasoning framework, not an empirical measurement yet.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a conceptual boundary-strength score B(i,j) = w_L*D_L + w_I*D_I + w_C*D_C + w_O*D_O + w_T*D_T over five divergence dimensions (language, invariants, lifecycle, ownership, change-rate), explicitly stated as 'not intended as a literal automated formula yet' but as a disciplined way of thinking, renamed a semantic distance d_sem(BC_i,BC_j) where small distance suggests splitting may be unnecessary and large distance justifies a boundary; immediately warns against false precision -- a specific numeric value like d_sem=0.73 is not scientifically meaningful absent a validated measurement procedure -- boxing that the formula is a reasoning framework, not yet an empirical measurement, and distinguishing formal construct from operational measure from empirical validation, of which only the first currently exists for this metric.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 206.21 Anti-Corruption Layer ... AssessmentResult -ACL-> Qualification. ... 206.22 Published Language ... Stable + Minimal + Versioned. ... 206.23 Open Host Service ... 206.24 Shared Kernel ... Share only what is genuinely semantically identical. Not merely convenient.
b_rows_sample.statement: Applies four standard DDD context-mapping patterns to the candidate bounded-context map: an Anti-Corruption Layer translating Assessment's AssessmentResult into Governance's Qualification without forcing either context to adopt the other's terminology; a Published Language for legitimately shared concepts (e.g. AssessmentReference), required to be stable, minimal, and versioned, never the complete internal model; an Open Host Service exposing semantic capabilities (not database structure) to many downstream consumers; and a Shared Kernel considered only for truly universal concepts (Identity, Version, CorrelationId, Timestamp), with an explicit warning that a shared kernel creates coupling, boxed as 'share only what is genuinely semantically identical, not merely convenient.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: 206.25 The identity question ... EntityId != CurrentState ... 206.26 Historical state ... CurrentState_t = pi(History_{<=t}). The projection may intentionally forget information. ... 206.27 Forgetting is therefore a first-class phenomenon ... Actor knowledge subset System memory subset Reality.
b_rows_sample.statement: Derives an architectural distinction from a Gita-lens observation about continuous identity across changing embodied states: EntityId != CurrentState, since an entity can pass through S1->S2->S3 without becoming a different entity -- explicitly framed as a conceptual lens reinforcing a DDD distinction, not a metaphysical claim ('not a proof of reincarnation'). Extends this with a second observation (a new state does not necessarily possess the knowledge of previous states): CurrentState_t = pi(History_{<=t}), where the projection pi may intentionally forget information, making 'forgetting' a first-class architectural phenomenon; derives the three-level epistemic hierarchy Actor-knowledge subset-or-equal System-memory subset-or-equal Reality, proposed as a recurring architectural principle. Explicitly guards against collapsing the analogy into identity, boxing the rule chain 'philosophical analogy -> architectural question -> formal model' and stating 'we should never write KnowledgeOS is Krishna'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 206.29 "What to do and what not to do" ... Evidence != Policy ... Probability != Obligation ... 206.31 AI consequence ... Prediction -> Assessment -> Governance -> Decision -> Action. ... 206.32 Inference has no implicit authority.
b_rows_sample.statement: Derives, again via the Gita-Chapter-4 lens, the Description-versus-Prescription distinction (what is, versus what ought to be done), placing Evidence on the descriptive/epistemic side and Policy on the prescriptive/governance side, boxing Evidence != Policy and Probability != Obligation as extremely important boundaries for AI systems; formalizes Decision = f(Evidence, Probability, Utility, Policy, Authority, Context) as the bridge between statistics and DDD governance; and states the AI consequence that a high-confidence model prediction (e.g. 0.87) does not by itself authorize an action -- the correct chain is Prediction -> Assessment -> Governance -> Decision -> Action -- boxing the critical KnowledgeOS principle 'Inference has no implicit authority': an AI system can assess, but cannot acquire authority merely because its confidence is high.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 206.34 Context boundary verdict ... Strong: Evidence, Assessment, Governance, Execution. Strong but requires further analysis: Decision, Observation. Cross-cutting rather than context: Identity, Lineage, Versioning, Correlation. Not yet justified as separate context: Model. ... 206.35 Important architectural caution ... BoundedContext != Microservice.
b_rows_sample.statement: Delivers a graded verdict over the seven candidate contexts: Evidence, Assessment, Governance, and Execution classified Strong; Decision and Observation classified Strong-but-requires-further-analysis; Identity/Lineage/Versioning/Correlation reclassified as cross-cutting concerns rather than contexts in their own right; and Model classified not yet justified as a separate context pending examination of the actual model registry and lifecycle. Adds the explicit architectural caution that a bounded context is not required to become a microservice -- it may be implemented as a module, package, component, service, or deployment unit -- boxing BoundedContext != Microservice as the DDD boundary and the deployment boundary are separate decisions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 206.36 Current architectural synthesis ... Concepts -> Meaning -> Relations -> StateSpaces -> Transitions -> Invariants -> Aggregates -> BoundedContexts -> ContextMap. This is an important methodological achievement. We are no longer designing from technology downward. We are deriving architecture from semantics upward. ... 206.37 Step 206 verdict DDD PASS, Mathematics PASS, Statistics PASS, Governance PASS, Gita lens CONSISTENT.
b_rows_sample.statement: Closes Step 206 by stating the full methodological derivation chain achieved so far: Concepts -> Meaning -> Relations -> StateSpaces -> Transitions -> Invariants -> Aggregates -> BoundedContexts -> ContextMap, characterized as deriving architecture from semantics upward rather than designing from technology downward; issues a per-discipline verdict, all PASS (DDD: boundaries derived from semantic difference not technical decomposition; Mathematics: state-space/transition relationships coherent; Statistics: uncertainty/inference kept distinct from normative decisions; Governance: policy/authority kept distinct from evidence/prediction) plus the Gita lens rated CONSISTENT, reaffirming Identity!=State, Knowledge!=Action, Description!=Prescription, CurrentKnowledge!=CompleteHistory. Immediately opens Step 207 (Context Contracts), tasked with deriving the semantic contracts along six directed edges of the loop (Evidence->Assessment->Governance->Decision->Execution->Observation->Evidence), each requiring Input/Meaning/Version/Preconditions/Guarantees/FailureSemantics/Lineage/Authority.

b_rows_sample.anchor: STEP 052 ... The strongest DDD file in the batch. section52.19's boundary test ("Each context should answer: What does this context have authority to change? If the answer is: Everything, the boundary is wrong") is a genuine, applicable heuristic. ... boxed KnowledgeOS != God Context
b_rows_sample.statement: Credits step-052 (Mathematical Kernel to DDD Bounded Context Mapping) as the strongest DDD file in the 041-055 batch: proposes seven candidate contexts (Evidence, Semantic, Knowledge, Causal, Decision, Governance, Learning) at an explicitly candidate (not final) level, gives a genuinely applicable boundary heuristic ('what does this context have authority to change -- if everything, the boundary is wrong'), a mathematical aggregate-boundary criterion, and explicit God-Context/God-Aggregate warnings, boxing KnowledgeOS != God Context and Agent-identity != Knowledge-identity. Flags one internal inconsistency (VD-13): the seven-context table (section 52.18) and the accompanying diagram (section 52.67, which adds ACTION and OUTCOME as first-class boxes) disagree with each other on the decomposition within the same file, and no context is assigned sole ownership of Identity despite step-048's I4 requiring exactly one authoritative owner per invariant.

b_notations: where does the meaning of a word change?

a_rows_sample.anchor: AIP is the PublicDigit AI Engineering Platform
a_rows_sample.statement: AIP is defined as a session-based, registry-first engineering operating model governing how AI-assisted engineering work is initiated, authorised, executed, verified, and closed inside .claude/, so that work is governed, traceable and auditable via the registry-first workflow. Its own operating instructions state: 'The product always has priority over the platform,' and Product Primacy (AIP-14) records that the platform is never the core domain -- every implementation decision answers 'How does this help implement the next PublicDigit feature?'

a_rows_sample.anchor: AIP is a socio-technical operating system for engineering
a_rows_sample.statement: Structural reading: AIP's current implemented core is a workflow/authority engine plus guard surfaces -- not a product domain. The product it serves (the election/voting platform, the KnowledgeOS body of knowledge) is outside AIP; AIP governs the process of building it, not the product itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Registry-first authority ... An asset that cannot answer them 'shall not be registered'
a_rows_sample.statement: Registry-first workflow (binding): (1) register with full traceability, (2) review/approve the registry entry, (3) implement, (4) verify against registered intent. Every asset answers five questions (R-17): capability -> bounded context -> architecture principle -> platform decision -> ADR; an asset that cannot answer them 'shall not be registered -- and shall not exist.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Every invariant BC-7 (the workflow engine) owns is mechanically enforced; almost every invariant outside BC-7 is declared only
a_rows_sample.statement: Headline structural finding -- the invariant asymmetry: assurance is strong where it is executable (BC-7) and weak where it is prose (outside BC-7). 'The platform mechanically protects orchestration, and protects knowledge/verification/communication only by declaration.' Stated as the single most important structural property of AIP's current architecture.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Core workflows ... Integrations
a_rows_sample.statement: Four core workflows: registry-first construction (register->approve->implement->verify); governed lane workflow (REGISTER->...->COMPLETE/FAIL/CANCEL with mutation-owner/START-stickiness invariants); the operating loop (Business capability -> ... -> KnowledgeOS promotion check); construction discipline (one objective, one approved plan, one completion review, one stopping point). Integrations: hooks wired via settings.json at five runtime moments; tests pin the workflow-engine contracts; persistence = runtime workflow records + session logs + docs/ governed artifacts; the registry is consumed at START/ON_DEMAND, human docs generated from it never the reverse; drafting studio consumes frozen templates by reference (no parallel copies).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Owns / Consumes / Produces / Explicitly does NOT own
a_rows_sample.statement: Owns: the workflow/authority engine (AST-015) and session-assignment resolver (AST-016); the registry (AST-009); the guard surface; session-continuity assets; the platform operating doctrine; ownership of mechanically-enforced invariants (I-1,I-2,I-3,G-1,G-2). Consumes: human authority acts (humanActRef); frozen product/document templates by reference; docs/ governed knowledge; the runtime/workflow/* records it reads and extends. Produces: the authority record; session/fact logs; guard-reminder signals and blocking gate verdicts; registry-driven configuration and generated documentation; verification reports/findings/decision records/acceptance records. Explicitly does NOT own: the product domain (AIP-14 Product Primacy); knowledge governance (BC-1 NOT BUILT); adversarial review automation (deferred, human); policy enforcement as a distinct capability (C-14 CONTESTED); knowledge distribution as an established capability (C-10 NOT YET ESTABLISHED); communication composition as a bounded context (C-19 stewardship, not a BC); the product's runtime/execution state.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the PKS<->AIP boundary is UNKNOWN in the current AIP corpus and is left to Stage 4
a_rows_sample.statement: AIP's evidence records the ARB 'Platform =^ Adoption separation' observation (platform concepts and PublicDigit adoption evidence interwoven in the same documents; separation expected to be driven by the first successful adoption in another project) and distinguishes the platform layer (.claude/) from the domain being built. Beyond these self-declarations, the PKS<->AIP boundary, and which side of the split EKS/PKS occupy relative to AIP, are explicitly left UNKNOWN to Stage 4 (not performed in this session).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge-concern vs platform-concern -- candidate split (evidence/finding, NOT decided)
a_rows_sample.statement: Candidate split (not decided): Knowledge concern (BC-1 NOT BUILT; Knowledge Engineer adopted-role-only); Assurance concern (BC-3/BC-4, partial/missing); Platform/mechanical concern (BC-7, workflow engine, registry -- fully implemented, A); Communication concern (C-10 NOT ESTABLISHED, C-19 stewardship, Communication Engineer nervous-system framing in unadopted history -- F/G). OQ-D (the EKP/PKS boundary) is explicitly OPEN -- deliberately not decided.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Headline structural findings
a_rows_sample.statement: Seven headline findings: (1) AIP is a registry-first, session-based engineering operating platform, not a product domain; (2) the implemented core is the workflow/authority engine plus guard surfaces, with knowledge/review components deferred/not built and verification under construction; (3) the invariant asymmetry is the load-bearing structural property; (4) the authority record lives in an ignored runtime directory (the durability inversion), decided-but-not-executed; (5) the D1/D2 decision state is contradictory across the corpus, surfaced not reconciled; (6) four unowned capabilities form one control loop with C-10/C-14 existence UNDECIDED; (7) AIP self-records four capability failures (EKS-01..04) -- the platform observing its own uneven assurance.

a_rows_sample.anchor: UNKNOWN entries
a_rows_sample.statement: 12 recorded UNKNOWNs (U-1..U-12): C-10 existence NOT YET ESTABLISHED; C-14 existence CONTESTED; the D1/D2 act-sequence UNKNOWN; whether the six-role model maps to any platform service/agent NOT ESTABLISHED; the EKP/PKS boundary OPEN; the knowledge-vs-platform-concern boundary UNDECIDED; AST-016 V-3 remedy UNDECIDED; C-5 access/artifact isolation and organisational independence NOT_ESTABLISHED; the four forbidden pairings ALL OPEN; EKS's/PKS's place relative to AIP UNKNOWN (left to Stage 4); the full MIGRATION-PLAN body RESOLVED by erratum E-3; whether KOS-AIP-GOV-STATE-DURABILITY-DECISION.md exists -- NOT PRODUCED.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Landscape integration -- which EKS/PKS/AIP responsibilities already exist, and where their boundaries lie
a_rows_sample.statement: Nine landscape findings (C-1..C-10 evidence) mapped onto the register, with F2/F3/F4 carry-forwards honored (implemented mechanism != domain ownership; evidence is current-state-scoped not universal; consumption != ownership != KnowledgeOS): state-as-fold/append-only log (C-2, SAME as Revisability-001's enforcement, mechanism layer); forward-only supersession (C-5, SAME as Revisability-001, asymmetric ownership PKS-governance/EKS-mechanism/AIP-declared-only); closed-verdict vocabulary (C-3, SAME as the Validation Layer, a published-language boundary); assessment-conferring-no-authority (C-4, SAME as INV-003 Established); epistemic-class discipline (C-8, SAME as Pramana-001's source-role separation, PKS-owned, asymmetric F3); regenerable non-authoritative projection (C-7, SAME as INV-004 Established); honest-UNKNOWN (C-10, SAME as H-ZERO-001, 'discipline, not mechanism'); authority-as-recorded-reference (C-1, SAME as the Authority family's core, X-02 SAME-vs-RELATED across systems UNKNOWN/U-02); the F4 relationship question (AIP is DISTINCT -- a consumer/runtime, not the owner, not the KnowledgeOS layer itself).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Platform Lifecycle (Idea→Knowledge→PKS→Implementation→Evidence→Evolution) ... B-1 correction: software→evidence OBSERVED · back-edge n≈3 informal / ≈2 formal · KnowledgeOS→PKS n=0 · Genesis has NO route
b_rows_sample.statement: The platform lifecycle is graded link-by-link: software-to-evidence is observed; the back-edge is n≈3 informal / ≈2 formal; KnowledgeOS-to-PKS generation is n=0; and the Genesis stage has no route at all. Individual grades are confirmed; the loop as a whole remains a hypothesis.

b_rows_sample.anchor: PKS Boundary — P1 method/binding/evidence ... I-7 (PKS never contains reusable method — stated AND breached)
b_rows_sample.statement: P1 defines PKS content as method/binding/evidence (cognate of Round38C-04); I-7 states a PKS never contains reusable method, yet this rule is both stated and breached in the current corpus. PKS contains artifacts; a projection claim is falsified for existing artifacts (authored, ARB-endorsed 9.9/10). The boundary rule is confirmed; the breach remains open, routed to D-8.

b_rows_sample.anchor: What does not survive — registers' contents · all records/reports · every PKS instance · Round-corpus case law · governed-registers.yaml · .claude/settings.json · election domain knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Elements that do NOT survive removal of the single product: registers' contents, all records/reports, every PKS instance, Round-corpus case law, governed-registers.yaml, .claude/settings.json, and election domain knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: R-6 | KnowledgeOS —creates→ PKS | UNIQUE — the loop's first edge is unproven inside and outside
b_rows_sample.statement: Relationship R-6: KnowledgeOS creates PKS. External support: scaffolding/generators (Spring Initializr-class) are implementation guidance only; context-engineering platforms that auto-assemble context are adjacent. Challenge: no external instance of generating a governed knowledge space is found; internally n=0. Confidence: UNIQUE — the loop's first edge is unproven both inside and outside the corpus.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Corrections applied to the concept matrix — PKS = Context Engineering softened
b_rows_sample.statement: Three corrections applied to the (external) concept matrix: (1) 'PKS = Context Engineering' softened to 'PKS addresses the same problem space as context engineering and extends it with governance, lifecycle, authority and engineering semantics' — not an identity claim, since the governed form has no demonstrated external instance; (2) Jansen & Bosch elevated to primary validation, since it validates the PROBLEM (knowledge vaporizes), and problem validation outranks solution fashion (Gartner-era context engineering); (3) the admission rule adopted as a standing header rule on both matrices.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The relationship pass sharpens the concept pass's conclusion: the platform's EDGES are almost all standard engineering — what is uniquely unproven is ONE edge (creates → PKS) and ONE layer name (DP-n)
b_rows_sample.statement: Aggregate result: externally supported (>=HIGH) relationships are R-3, R-4, R-5, R-8, R-10, and R-2's separation; medium relationships are R-1, R-7, R-9; the unique, operationally-unproven items are R-6 (creates->PKS) and DP-n as a named layer. The distinctive bet of KnowledgeOS is now precisely locatable as R-6; everything else is either validated or a naming choice, and R-6 is exactly what the charter's gated stages and the docket's doors already refuse to assume.

b_rows_sample.anchor: REV 2 — R-6 BROADENED per review: the bet is the INTEGRATION, not one edge
b_rows_sample.statement: Challenge accepted: 'KnowledgeOS is not merely a generator. It is the platform that governs the ENTIRE PKS lifecycle.' R-6 is restated as a composite chain: KnowledgeOS discovers/models/governs/generates/evolves PKS, guides PRODUCT ENGINEERING (the actor — work, not magic), which engineers software, collects evidence, and improves KnowledgeOS. The actor (product engineering) was already implicit in the work-execution progressions (P-7/P-8) and 'the producing track' as records-owner, but the composite chain had omitted it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: PKS — governed, machine-readable context for AI ... "context engineering" 2025–26
b_rows_sample.statement: PKS as governed, machine-readable AI context converges with industry 'context engineering' (Gartner July 2025: 'context engineering is in, prompt engineering is out', predicted in 80% of AI tools by 2028); enterprise practice defines governed, machine-readable context any AI agent can use reliably. Challenge: the field is platform-vendor-led, young, terminology unstable. Confidence: HIGH for the need; the governance framing (authority, lifecycle, bindings) remains rarer and partially ours.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The enforcement finding (governed context + advisory capabilities) ... 86% of enterprises are assembling rich, semantically grounded context — and handing it over with no governance
b_rows_sample.statement: The industry-wide finding that 86% of enterprises assemble rich context but hand it over with no governance over agent actions, and 89% say governance is critical while ~50% have it, is convergent with this platform's own governed-context-plus-advisory-capabilities gap. Confidence: HIGH.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS→PKS generation (n=0) ... UNIQUE HYPOTHESIS — operational proof only
b_rows_sample.statement: KnowledgeOS generating a PKS (n=0) has only adjacent external support (context-engineering platforms generate context from metadata, not the same as generating a governed PKS); it remains a unique hypothesis needing operational proof only.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Canonical concept glossary — the 14 examined, plus 3 the corpus forces in
b_rows_sample.statement: A 17-row glossary assigns each term (KnowledgeOS, PKS, Engineering Knowledge, Engineering Capability, Engineering Method, Engineering Governance, Engineering Runtime, Runtime Adapter, Engineering Evidence, Engineering Ontology, Documentation Ontology L-A, Platform Ontology L-B, Product Ontology L-C, Knowledge Graph, Engineering Kernel, Knowledge Space, Design Policy DP-n, Execution Asset AST-nnn) one meaning, owner, protected invariant, place, and verdict (KEEP/REJECTED-MERGED/SPLIT/CANDIDATE). Success criterion: every major engineering term gets one meaning, one owner, one place.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Concept relationships — the reviewer's example chain, validated ... KnowledgeOS creates PKS contains Engineering Knowledge organized by Ontology used by Capabilities executed through Runtime produces Evidence improves KnowledgeOS
b_rows_sample.statement: The proposed chain is validated edge by edge: 'KnowledgeOS creates PKS' is a hypothesis (n=0, every PKS is authored by a person); 'PKS contains Engineering Knowledge' is WRONG, violating I-7 (a PKS contains product knowledge and bindings; reusable method must not live in it — the current breach is the exception that proves the rule); 'knowledge organized by Ontology' holds with the precision that L-A organizes artifacts/carriers, not knowledge itself (I-1); 'used by Capabilities' holds (capabilities may read across space boundaries, never own — H-1); 'Capabilities executed through Runtime' is imprecise (capabilities are advisory scripts invoked on demand; the runtime executes Execution Assets/ASTs; 41 enforced controls live runtime-side while every capability is advisory — the drawn edge hides this finding); 'Runtime produces Evidence' should attribute production to WORK (P-7/P-8), the runtime only hosts the work; 'Evidence improves KnowledgeOS' is only partly true (n≈3 informal, B-1's fact).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Two corrections to the Addendum's own positioning ... "KnowledgeOS is a Core Domain" ... Contradicts a DA ruling
b_rows_sample.statement: Two corrections to an Addendum's positioning: (1) 'KnowledgeOS is a Core Domain' contradicts AIP-14/DA ruling 2026-07-27 that the Election System is the Core Domain and the platform is a Supporting Subdomain; the Reference Model records only the conditional (engineering knowledge would be Core Domain if the gate opened, and it has not). (2) 'PKS is a generated projection' was falsified last round: existing PKS artifacts carry Status: ACCEPTED WITH REFINEMENTS, a Commission, and ARB endorsement 9.9/10 — they are authored, not derived.

b_rows_sample.anchor: W-3 · "PKS is a projection" — FALSIFIED for every existing PKS artifact
b_rows_sample.statement: The claim 'PKS is a projection' is falsified for every existing PKS artifact: examined fields (Authority: Generated, human-asserted; Status: ACCEPTED WITH REFINEMENTS; a Disposition History with ARB reviewer endorsement 9.9/10; a Commission) are incompatible with a projection, which would carry authority:derived (machine-checkable), no acceptance (regenerated, not accepted), a source and regeneration command, and no Commission. A mechanical grep for authority:derived|generated across docs/pks, docs/knowledgeos, docs/implementation returns 10 files, every one a prose mention of the vocabulary, not an application of it — those paths sit outside knowledge-schema.yaml's declared scope.include. This sharpens a prior Ontology Classification finding ('blocked in practice') to stronger: existing PKS artifacts are positively authoritative — authored, commissioned, reviewed, disposed, and accepted — incompatible with 'derived'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Assurance composition tree and cascading invalidation
a_rows_sample.statement: Revisits assurance composition: assurance objects A1,A2,A3 may be combined by decision policy as A1 and A2 and A3, but each A_i itself carries Validity, Provenance, Confidence and Scope, so assurance composition is hierarchical -- depicted as an assurance tree (Decision -> Assurance A/Assurance B -> Claim/Evidence -> Validation). Cascading invalidation: if Evidence(E) is revoked, Claim(C) may become invalid, then Assurance(A) must be recomputed, then potentially Decision(D) must be revisited.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Affected(E)=Descendants(E,G_P); incremental assurance recomputation
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes dependency closure as Affected(E) = Descendants(E, G_P) (an evidence revocation propagates through the provenance/dependency graph G_P), and states as a major software property that KnowledgeOS should support incremental assurance recomputation -- it should not need to recompute the entire knowledge base after every change.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Assurance monotonicity is not universally true; non-monotonic knowledge revision
a_rows_sample.statement: Considers the candidate property 'adding valid evidence should not reduce assurance unnecessarily' and rejects it as not universally true, since new evidence can reveal that previous beliefs were wrong -- so Knowledge is not necessarily monotonic: K_t |= A can hold while K_{t+1} not|= A after new evidence, which 'is not a failure, it is knowledge revision'. Consequently Assurance_{t+1}(A) < Assurance_t(A) is a supported, expected transition. Safety is treated as different: a safety invariant should be monotonic in the sense that once a prohibited state is detected the system should not ignore it because new evidence is favorable, though the underlying factual interpretation may change -- so a SafetyDecision must retain the evidence and reasoning that produced it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Twelve falsification experiments for Step 42 (all PASS)

b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the epistemic minimality criterion: two candidate epistemic states are indistinguishable with respect to a mandatory epistemic operation set iff every operation in that set produces the same observable result for both states across all valid inputs; if some mandatory operation distinguishes them, they cannot be collapsed into one state.

b_rows_sample.anchor: $$\boxed{Unknown\ required}$$ ... Unknown does not mean false. $$Unknown(p) \neq Refuted(p)$$ Nor does it mean that no observation exists. An observation may exist while remaining insufficient to establish the proposition.
b_rows_sample.statement: Derives Unknown as a required epistemic distinction (there is no sufficient epistemic basis to classify p as supported or refuted, distinguishable via Assess), and clarifies Unknown does not mean false, nor does it mean no observation exists — an observation may exist while remaining insufficient.

b_rows_sample.anchor: $$E^+ \models p$$ and $$E^- \models \neg p$$ Then both support and refutation are simultaneously present. ... $$\boxed{Conflict\ required}$$ This is a mathematical necessity under the mandatory operation set.
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues Conflict is a mathematically necessary fourth epistemic state: when independently qualified evidence sets simultaneously support p (E+ |= p) and refute p (E- |= not-p), a three-state model {Unknown,Supported,Refuted} would have to arbitrarily choose one, losing information relevant to DetectContradiction and Resolve; hence a distinct Conflict state is required.

b_rows_sample.anchor: $$\boxed{Missingness\ is\ required\ information}$$ but: $$\boxed{Missingness\ need\ not\ be\ a\ value\ of\ the\ epistemic\ status}$$ This is precisely where the earlier formulations risked overloading Sigma.
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes Missing (no observation obtained) from Unknown (observation obtained but insufficient) as causally different histories relevant to data quality, evidence qualification, and audit, but concludes Missingness need not be a top-level value of the epistemic status Sigma itself -- it can be represented at the evidence/observation layer instead, correcting a risk of Sigma overload in earlier formulations.

b_rows_sample.statement: Establishes three orthogonal dimension separations: Supersession is a lifecycle/history relation, not an epistemic status (EpistemicState != LifecycleState); Authorization/Approval belong to a governance model, not the epistemic status (EpistemicState != GovernanceState); Contested and Resolution are process/workflow states derivable from Conflict+Assessment+Authority/Context rather than primitive Sigma values; Validity (Current/Stale/Expired) is temporal/contextual semantics, not epistemic status.

b_rows_sample.anchor: $$\boxed{\Sigma_0 = \{Unknown, Supported, Refuted, Conflict\}}$$ ... $$\Sigma_0(p) = (S(p),R(p))$$ produces four states ... $$\boxed{\Sigma_0 \cong \{0,1\}^2}$$
b_rows_sample.statement: Constructs Sigma_0 formally as the pair (S(p), R(p)) of binary support-qualified and refutation-qualified indicators, giving the isomorphism Sigma_0 ≅ {0,1}^2 with (0,0)=Unknown, (1,0)=Supported, (0,1)=Refuted, (1,1)=Conflict — a mathematical construction rather than a mere four-label proposal.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose we remove one state. ### Remove Unknown ... Invalid. ### Remove Supported ... Invalid. ### Remove Refuted ... Invalid. ### Remove Conflict ... Invalid. Therefore: $$\boxed{|\Sigma_0|\geq4}$$ ... $$\boxed{|\Sigma_0|=4}$$
b_rows_sample.statement: Proves minimality of the four-state structure by exhaustive deletion: removing any one of Unknown/Supported/Refuted/Conflict leaves some (S,R) combination unrepresentable, which breaks a mandatory operation's output (e.g. removing Conflict destroys DetectContradiction's output for the (1,1) case). Concludes |Sigma_0| >= 4 is forced and, since four states are sufficient, |Sigma_0| = 4 exactly.

b_rows_sample.anchor: $$\boxed{Supported \equiv QualifiedSupport > 0}$$ ... $$\Sigma_0$$ is an epistemic assessment structure, not a truth-value algebra. ... $$\boxed{Uncertainty \notin \Sigma_0}$$ ... $$\boxed{\Sigma_0\ does\ not\ require\ probability}$$ Do not introduce probability merely because uncertainty exists.
b_rows_sample.statement: Three qualifications on the derived structure: (1) Supported/Refuted are not truth values (Supported does not mean p=True); they mean QualifiedSupport/QualifiedRefutation exceed zero under some policy-dependent assessment. (2) Uncertainty/confidence does not need to be a fifth primitive Sigma value -- two Supported assertions can differ in confidence without requiring different epistemic categories, represented instead via an associated Assessment/Uncertainty function. (3) No probability space is required or implied by any of the four states; the methodological rule stated is 'do not introduce probability merely because uncertainty exists.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: $$State(p) = (\Sigma_E(p), \Lambda(p), \Gamma(p), Context(p))$$ rather than one overloaded status enum. This is a major result of the derivation. ... $$\boxed{\Sigma \perp \Lambda \perp \Gamma}$$ conceptually, even though operations may use all three. Here perp means distinct semantic dimensions, not statistical independence.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the overall knowledge-object state as a 4-tuple State(p) = (Sigma_E(p), Lambda(p), Gamma(p), Context(p)) -- epistemic, lifecycle, governance, context -- rather than one overloaded status enum, described as a major result. States Sigma perp Lambda perp Gamma, explicitly clarifying that perp here denotes distinct semantic dimensions (an architectural/ontological claim), not statistical independence (a measurement claim) -- a terminology caution against conflating the two senses of 'independent'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: $$\sigma_1\sqcup\sigma_2 = (s_1\lor s_2,\ r_1\lor r_2)$$ ... $$Supported\sqcup Refuted=Conflict$$ ... $$Conflict\sqcup anything=Conflict$$ ... this is a derived candidate algebra, not yet proof that all KnowledgeOS merge semantics must use it.
b_rows_sample.statement: Derives a join-semilattice merge operation over Sigma_0: sigma1 ⊔ sigma2 = (s1 OR s2, r1 OR r2), giving Unknown⊔Supported=Supported, Supported⊔Refuted=Conflict, Conflict⊔anything=Conflict, making Conflict the top element and Unknown the bottom of the {0,1}^2 lattice. Explicitly caveated as a derived candidate algebra requiring separate testing against the actual corpus/implementation before being treated as required merge semantics.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ATTACK 9 — Is OR-MERGE mandated, or merely convenient? *** THE DECISIVE ONE *** ... If Sigma is STORED and merged with OR: state stays (1,1) (Conflict) FOREVER — OR is monotone, so no merge can ever clear the R bit. If Sigma is DERIVED from the evidence set: state correctly becomes Supported. **LANDS — and it decides D-4.** OR-merge is correct ONLY IF Sigma is DERIVED from the evidence set. A STORED Sigma under OR-merge cannot recover from Retract, contradicting 272B's own operation set.
b_rows_sample.statement: ATTACK 9 (marked 'THE DECISIVE ONE') lands and directly resolves decision D-4 (is Sigma stored or derived?): OR-based merge (sigma1 ⊔ sigma2 = (s1∨s2, r1∨r2)) is monotone, so if Sigma is stored as accumulated state, a Refute-then-Retract sequence (evidence e1=Support, e2=Refute reaching Conflict, then Retract(e2)) leaves the stored value permanently at Conflict since OR can never clear a bit -- yet Step 272B's own operation set includes Retract, and correctly recomputing Sigma from the current evidence set after Retract gives Supported, not Conflict. Conclusion: Sigma must be DERIVED (recomputed from the live evidence set) rather than stored/accumulated, or the theory contradicts its own Retract operation.

ℛ = ℛ_sup ⊎ ℛ_ref ⊎ ℛ_der ⊎ ℛ_supp ⊎ ℛ_res ⊎ ℛ_rel ; DAGs: sup, ref, der non-transitive: supp, res symmetric: rel ; DERIVED, never stored: Σ · equals · contradicts · conflictsWith ; EXTERNAL: History · Policy · Autho

F(Hr) = F(Hs) = True ... i = relate(A1,A4,supersedes) -> congruent: True ... i = assert A2 -> congruent: True ... i = relate(A4,A1,refines) -> congruent: True ... a_rows_sample.statement: Structural (by-construction) explanation for why congruence held in every test: T's derived signature K x Op x Policy x Authority -harpoon-> K x Outcome does not include History in its domain, so T cannot depend on it — a function cannot depend on an argument it does not receive. This holds under exactly two assumptions: A1 (T reads only K, Policy, Authority — PROVEN by elimination of actor/time/evidence/context during signature derivation) and A2 (no operation consults order-of-arrival — HOLDS for the twelve derived operations because A and R are sets, making order structurally unobservable).

a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit forward-looking design constraint: assumption A2 (no operation consults insertion order) is violable by future design — any future operation implementing 'first assertion wins' or 'most recently added is authoritative' semantics would break congruence immediately; the theory now states this as an explicit constraint rather than a silent assumption.

a_rows_sample.anchor: SUFFICIENT UNDER ASSUMPTIONS. Not sufficient unqualified: the assumptions are real and A2 is violable by future design. Not insufficient: no counterexample exists and none can, given A1. Not unknown: the test was constructed correctly and executed.
a_rows_sample.statement: Final classification: the Knowledge-State/History sufficiency question is SUFFICIENT UNDER ASSUMPTIONS — deliberately neither 'sufficient unqualified' (the assumptions A1/A2 are real and A2 is violable), nor 'insufficient' (no counterexample exists, and none can given A1), nor 'unknown' (the test was validly constructed and executed).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge State is sufficient for FUTURE COMPUTATION. It is NOT sufficient for GOVERNANCE AUDIT. ... Who asserted this, and when? NO ... Was every admission properly authorised? NO — GovernanceValid(K,Γ) needs History ... What did we believe last March? NO — needs History
a_rows_sample.statement: The state/history sufficiency boundary is drawn precisely: K alone answers what is currently held, what follows from an operation (congruence), whether structural/semantic invariants hold, and current epistemic status (recomputable from e); K alone CANNOT answer who asserted something and when, whether every admission was properly authorised (GovernanceValid(K,Gamma) needs History), or what was believed at a past point in time (needs History or a bitemporal interpretation of t).

a_rows_sample.anchor: K answers what is known. History answers how it came to be known and by whom. Neither reduces to the other, and T needs only the first.
a_rows_sample.statement: Governing principle stated as the resolution of the state/history boundary the programme has circled since the executed History(K)!=K counterexample: K answers what is known; History answers how it came to be known and by whom; neither reduces to the other, and the transformation function T needs only K.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Proposition | A meaningful statement that can be true or false. | P=(Entity,Dimension,Value) ... Assertion | A proposition put forward as true, with a specific epistemic status... Knowledge | An assertion that satisfies the epistemic criteria for knowledge (justified true belief)
b_rows_sample.statement: Splits the Knowledge Atom into a three-level hierarchy Proposition subset-of Assertion subset-of Knowledge: Proposition=(E,D,V) is content without commitment; Assertion=(P,Sigma,Evidence,tau,Provenance) is a proposition put forward as true; Knowledge=(A,Justification,True) is a justified-true assertion; corrects the earlier Knowledge Atom to actually be an Assertion, not raw Knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Who determines True? KnowledgeOS observes, reconstructs, compares, challenges and guides. It generally cannot access Truth itself... Truth \neq Truth Assessment
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects making absolute Truth an internal primitive of Knowledge, since KnowledgeOS cannot access Truth directly; replaces the three-level model with four levels (Proposition -> Assertion -> Epistemically Accepted -> Reality/Omega), where 'Knowledge' becomes K=(A,Justification,TruthAssessment) rather than requiring literal correspondence to reality.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Observation \rightarrow Candidate Proposition(s) ... because an observation can be ambiguous. ... 'Host responds on port 8081' -> P1/P2/P3
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects 'Observe -> Proposition' to 'Observation -> Candidate Proposition(s)', since one observation (e.g. a host responding on a port) can support multiple distinct, non-exclusive candidate propositions requiring Zero/Lord/Semantic-Reconstruction to disambiguate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t = \mathcal{E}_t(\mathcal{A}_t) ... Knowledge isn't necessarily one object. It is a state of knowledge over many propositions and assertions.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reframes Knowledge from a single giant tuple to a Knowledge State K_t = E_t(A_t), an epistemic evaluation function over the set of currently available assertions A_t, foreshadowing K_{t+1}=Update(K_t,Observation_t,Zero_t,Lord_t,Evidence_t).

b_rows_sample.anchor: X_t \rightarrow O_t \rightarrow R_t \rightarrow A_t \rightarrow K_t
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the too-simple Reality->Observation->Knowledge pipeline into X_t (domain/reality) -> O_t (observation) -> R_t (semantic reconstruction/interpretation) -> A_t (assertion) -> K_t (knowledge state), with the critical point Observation ≠ Interpretation ≠ Assertion ≠ Knowledge, illustrated with the Bhīṣma example (seeing him = observation; 'Bhīṣma is a person' = interpretation; 'Bhīṣma is Arjuna's grandfather' = assertion; the same claim with provenance and epistemic qualification = knowledge).

b_rows_sample.anchor: P = \text{a semantically evaluable claim about entities, relationships, states or events}
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes Proposition as a semantically evaluable claim (examples: IsOnBattlefield(Bhishma), GrandfatherOf(Bhishma,Arjuna), OpponentOf(Bhishma,Arjuna)), distinguished from Assertion: Proposition ≠ Assertion, and Assertion = Proposition + Epistemic Qualification + Provenance. Flagged as a distinction that 'should be frozen'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A_3 = Inference( A_1,A_2,\ldots, Rule, Assumptions, Provenance )
b_rows_sample.statement: Extends Infer(A_1,A_2,Rule)->A_3 to require every derived assertion to carry Rule, Assumptions, and Provenance so KnowledgeOS can explain 'why do you believe this?': every derived assertion traceable to source assertions + inference rule + assumptions + context, called essential for deterministic assurance.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Document \neq Knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the naive Documents->Chunk->Embedding->VectorDB->RAG->LLM architecture as 'not KnowledgeOS' because it bypasses the epistemic model: a document is not knowledge but an information-bearing source from which observations/assertions may be constructed — Document ≠ Knowledge, Document ≠ Evidence — illustrated by Document->Observation->Candidate Assertion->Evidence->Knowledge State.

b_rows_sample.anchor: LLM\ Output \neq Knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Names three constitutional invariants for sources: (1) Source ≠ Knowledge (Document/API Response/Git Repository ≠ Knowledge); (2) LLM Output ≠ Knowledge — LLM Output -> Candidate Interpretation -> Epistemic Processing -> Knowledge; (3) Retrieval ≠ Knowledge Creation — Retrieve(Q) -> EvidenceCandidates -> Evaluate -> Knowledge. Overarching principle: 'Sources provide information; KnowledgeOS constructs governed knowledge from it. LLMs interpret; KnowledgeOS evaluates and governs. Retrieval supplies evidence candidates; it does not automatically create knowledge.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Interpret: Observation \times Context \rightarrow CandidateMeaning
b_rows_sample.statement: Interpret:Observation×Context->CandidateMeaning is where the structural parser, semantic parser, domain model, and LLM participate, worked through 'those with whom I have to fight' -> structural parsing -> semantic parsing -> candidate semantic structure -> candidate dimensions {Actor,Target,Action,Relationship,Obligation,Context} — explicitly 'not yet accepted knowledge'. CandidateAssertion=(Proposition,Sources,Interpretation,Context), e.g. 'Bhīṣma is Arjuna's grandfather' becomes a candidate proposition via Interpret->CandidateAssertions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Assess: CandidateAssertion \times Evidence \times Rules \times Context \rightarrow EpistemicAssessment
b_rows_sample.statement: Assess:CandidateAssertion×Evidence×Rules×Context->EpistemicAssessment produces Σ_A=(Acquisition,Support,Uncertainty,Validity) per explicit policy, contrasting e.g. (Acquisition=Reported,Support=Moderate,Uncertainty=Moderate,Validity=Current) against (Acquisition=AI-Generated,Support=None,Uncertainty=High,Validity=Unknown) depending on what actually supports the proposition. CandidateAssertion --Assessment--> Assertion=(P,E,Σ,Π,τ,C,ID); K_{t+1}=δ(K_t,A). Full acquisition chain: X->Artifact->Observation->Interpretation->CandidateAssertion->Assessment->Assertion->K_{t+1}, stated to be 'already a computable architecture'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \mathcal P = \mathcal P_F \cup \mathcal P_N \cup \mathcal P_Q \cup \mathcal P_H \cup \mathcal P_I \ldots
b_rows_sample.statement: After ten tests, provisionally establishes 'Source Observation is computationally realizable' across documents, DB results, internet resources, human statements, LLM outputs, code, rules, ADRs, constitutions and instructions, preserving Source event ≠ Meaning ≠ Assertion. Surfaces two explicit unresolved theoretical points without deciding them: Open Point A — whether one Proposition abstraction P_F∪P_N∪P_Q∪P_H∪P_I∪... (factual/normative/definitional/instructional/question/hypothesis/interpretation) with an explicit semantic type suffices, versus needing genuinely distinct object types; Open Point B — whether the Observation model should stay unified (with acquisition method/type recording measurement vs statement vs database vs LLM etc.) rather than creating separate Observation concepts per source class.

b_rows_sample.anchor: one Proposition abstraction, with explicit semantic type.
b_rows_sample.statement: Poses two explicit architectural-fork questions to the domain authority rather than deciding unilaterally: Question 1 — should factual/normative/definitional/instructional/hypothetical/interrogative content be different TYPES of semantic proposition under one common Proposition abstraction (recommended: Yes — one Proposition abstraction with explicit semantic type, rather than unrelated objects)? Question 2 — should the observation model stay unified, with acquisition method/type recording whether it came from measurement/database/document/human/LLM/API/parser (recommended: Yes)? If both are agreed, proposes formally closing Observation and moving to 'Computational Closure 2 — Interpretation', testing whether parsing+ontology+rules+LLM+human interpretation can transform arbitrary source observations into candidate semantic structures 'without pretending that interpretation is truth'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Should KnowledgeOS be allowed to create an Assertion with an explicitly unresolved epistemic state
b_rows_sample.statement: Poses and then answers the pivotal admission-boundary design choice: should an Assertion require passing a minimum admission threshold, or may it hold an explicitly unresolved epistemic state (Unknown/Hypothesized/WeaklySupported)? Recommends and then (in a 'Domain Authority' voice) DECIDES the latter: Assertion ≠ Proven Truth. Rationale given for rejecting the threshold alternative: it would remove Zero's ability to detect gaps (no representation for Unknown/Hypothesized), remove Lord's ability to generate candidates (no place for them to reside), sever the Observation->Interpretation->Candidate->Assertion provenance chain, damage auditability (no record of 'what we considered but did not accept'), make the incomplete-question problem unsolvable, collapse the Unknown-vs-Absent distinction, and break the learning trajectory Hypothesized->WeaklySupported->StronglySupported.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Truth = "This is what we currently represent, with this degree of support, uncertainty, and validity."
b_rows_sample.statement: Re-runs all eight test cases (DB result -> StronglySupported; unstructured document -> WeaklySupported; internet page -> WeaklySupported with caveats; human statement -> Reported; LLM output -> Hypothesized; incomplete question -> no assertion created, Zero detects gap, clarification requested; conflicting sources -> both assertions remain in the Knowledge State with a detected Conflict; unknown value -> Assertion(Unknown)) through the new admission model. States the redefined meaning of 'the single source of truth': Truth = 'this is what we currently represent, with this degree of support, uncertainty, and validity', NOT 'this is factually correct in reality' — the formalization of Knowledge ≠ Reality. Six constitutional invariants listed: Assertion≠Proven Truth; admission does not require verification; Unknown is a valid epistemic state (not absence of an assertion); epistemic status can evolve; multiple epistemic states can coexist (Conflicting is valid); provenance is preserved. Declares the Epistemic Admission Boundary computationally closed and proceeds to 'Computational Closure 3 — The Knowledge State'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A \not\equiv Truth(P)
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes Assertion A=(P,E,Σ,Π,τ,C,ID) with A≢Truth(P): A is 'KnowledgeOS's governed representation of P'. Two assertions of the identical proposition 'Nexus.version=3.69' can carry different epistemic states (Σ_A=(Observed,Strong,Low,Current) vs Σ_B=(Reported,Weak,High,Unknown)) and are 'not epistemically equivalent', giving Assertion⇏StrongEvidence, Assertion⇏Certainty, Assertion⇏Truth.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Admit(P,\Pi_1) \neq Admit(P,\Pi_2)
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces admission policy Π_adm with Admit(P_c,E,C,Π_adm)->{Assertion|Reject|Defer|RequestMoreEvidence}; admission is purpose-dependent, Admit(P,Π_1)≠Admit(P,Π_2) (an exploration policy may allow Weak support, a production-migration policy may require Strong support) — connecting directly to the Ideal State theory: an assertion can exist with Σ_K=Weak while the Ideal State requires Σ_I=Strong, producing a discrepancy rather than an invalid assertion. Distinguishes Admission ('may this proposition exist as governed knowledge?', Candidate->Assertion) from Validation ('does this assertion satisfy a particular requirement?', Assertion×Constraint->ValidationResult): Admission ≠ Validation — an assertion can be admitted (e.g. during discovery) yet later FAIL a validation (e.g. a migration requiring verified version) WITHOUT being deleted; it 'remains useful historical knowledge'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Assertion \in KnowledgeState ... KnowledgeState \neq SetOfAssertions
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects an earlier equation Assertion=Knowledge (too strong) to Assertion∈KnowledgeState while KnowledgeState≠SetOfAssertions: the Knowledge State is a structured object K_t=(Assertions,Evidence,Relationships,Conflicts,Gaps,Provenance,Context,History,Constraints), 'a structured state, not simply a bag of claims' — called 'an important DDD correction'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \text{Evidence is not a property of a document.}
b_rows_sample.statement: Central correction: Evidence is not a property of a document but 'a relationship between an observation and a proposition under a context and an evaluation rule' — Evidence(O,P,C,R). Prevents the mistake 'the document says X, therefore X is evidence [for whatever P]'. Gives Evidence≠Observation, Evidence≠Source, Evidence≠Support, Evidence≠Truth as four fundamental distinctions, and shows the SAME observation can be evidence for one proposition and not another (Evidence(O,P_1)≠Evidence(O,P_2)) — 'evidence is therefore relational'. E=(O,P,R,C,T,Q,Π): observation, target proposition, evaluation rule, context, temporal applicability, quality assessment, provenance.

type_signature.domain: observation x proposition x context x rule

b_rows_sample.anchor: Conclusion = Inference(Premises,Rule,Context)
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects 'the evidence voted for 3.69' informal aggregation, requiring Conclusion=Inference(Premises,Rule,Context) via an explicit inference rule (worked example: APIResponse.version=3.69 plus rule 'APIResponse(source=NexusProduction)=>CurrentVersion(NexusProduction)' yields the conclusion). Distinguishes four conclusion kinds: Deductive (Γ⊨P, entailed), Inductive (evidence increases support for a generalization without entailing it), Abductive (select the best explanation among hypotheses {H_1,...,H_n} — 'extremely relevant to KnowledgeOS'), Computational/derived (e.g. a version-vs-required-version comparison rule). Formalizes Conclusion object C_n=(P,Γ,R,κ,Σ,Π,t) (proposition, premises/evidence, inference rule, inference method, epistemic assessment, provenance, derivation time), letting KnowledgeOS answer 'why did you reach this conclusion?' not just 'what did you conclude?'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: VERDICT: the EKP's (𝒜,ℛ) is E — a bounded-context-specific model — and B — a representation. It is NOT C (a projection of the theory's K), because a projection cannot invent the fields it lacks. ... Therefore: ontology ≠ implementation representation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Central §5 verdict: the EKP's (A,R) is a bounded-context-specific model (category E) and a representation (category B), NOT a projection of the theory's K (category C), since a projection cannot invent fields it lacks; it is a different K over a different, non-epistemic assertion type (governed documents, not epistemic assertions); the mandate's central warning that ontology != implementation representation is thereby empirically demonstrated, not merely avoided — the two K's share shape (identified items + typed relations) but differ in carrier.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 4 of 9 reconstructible. The EKP is an adequate governance-document store and an inadequate epistemic store — and it was never built to be the latter.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reconstructibility audit: of §5's nine listed items, only context, supersession, identity, and governance boundaries are reconstructible from the EKP (4 of 9); epistemic qualification, evidence references, temporal validity, contradiction, and provenance are not — the EKP is an adequate governance-document store and an inadequate epistemic store, and was never built to be the latter.

a_rows_sample.anchor: a working knowledge platform was built without temporal validity, evidence, provenance or epistemic status. The theory must explain that omission, not ignore it. ... EKP's assertions are documents under governance ... the theory's assertions are claims under evidence, for which they do not [suffice]
a_rows_sample.statement: Most instructive fact of the artifact: a real working knowledge platform operates without temporal validity, evidence, provenance, or epistemic status fields, because its assertions are 'documents under governance' (for which lifecycle and authority suffice), whereas the theory's assertions are 'claims under evidence' (for which they do not) — the theory is obligated to explain this omission rather than dismiss it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: order of assertion YES ... actor YES ... wall-clock YES ... the assertions themselves NO ... asserted relations NO — executed counterexample (supersession vs independent observation) ... Σ YES — recomputable from e
a_rows_sample.statement: State-membership test (can two histories yield the same K while differing in X?), executed per row: order of assertion, actor, and wall-clock time can all differ between histories yielding the same K (all classified historical metadata, not state-defining); the assertions themselves and asserted relations cannot differ without changing K (state-defining, with an executed counterexample distinguishing supersession from independent observation); Sigma (epistemic status) can differ across histories yielding the same K because it is recomputable from evidence e (derivable, not state-defining).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Transformation-sufficiency test F(H1) = F(H2) ⇒ F(T(H1,i)) = F(T(H2,i)) — executed, congruent for every input tested. See artifact F.
a_rows_sample.statement: The transformation-sufficiency (congruence) test F(H1)=F(H2) => F(T(H1,i))=F(T(H2,i)) was executed and found congruent for every tested input, with full detail deferred to a separate artifact F — direct empirical support for the K=(A,R) abstraction passing the Step-259 congruence criterion.

a_rows_sample.anchor: object identity trivial ... structural equality (𝒜₁,ℛ₁) = (𝒜₂,ℛ₂) including Π — YES — equivalence relation proven ... semantic equivalence equal on (P,c,t), ignoring id,e,Π — YES ... observational equivalence agree on every Query — derived from structural ... history equivalence History(K₁) = Histor
a_rows_sample.statement: Identity test: five distinct identity/equality notions are all formally defined and (except trivial object identity) executed — structural equality (proven an equivalence relation), semantic equivalence (equal on (P,c,t), ignoring id/e/Pi), observational equivalence (agreement on every Query, derived from structural equality), and history equivalence (equality of History(K)); the containment order history equivalence properly-contains-in structural properly-contains-in semantic is established, and it is executed that History(K) != K (history is not part of the state).

a_rows_sample.anchor: a ∈ K ⟺ a ∈ 𝒜. Decidable, O(1). ℛ endpoints reference ids, so relation membership is (f,t,ty) ∈ ℛ with f,t ∈ ids(𝒜) — enforced by StructuralValid.
a_rows_sample.statement: Membership is defined and decidable in O(1): a is in K iff a is in the assertion set A; relation membership requires (from,to,type) in R with both endpoints being ids of members of A, enforced by a StructuralValid check.

a_rows_sample.anchor: D_VER = Dimension("Version", ...) A1=... A2=... A3=... A4=... K = ( {A1,A2,A3,A4}, {(8663022439, e2c73b5500, supersedes)} ) StructuralValid(K) = (True,'ok') SemanticallyValid(K) = (True,'ok'). The definition is complete: a finite valid K exists and was constructed.
a_rows_sample.statement: Construction test: an explicit finite Knowledge State K is built from four concrete Nexus-version assertions (with ids, evidence, context, temporal validity, and origin) plus one supersedes relation, and both StructuralValid(K) and SemanticallyValid(K) evaluate to (True,'ok') — demonstrating the definition is complete enough that a finite valid K actually exists and can be constructed, not merely postulated.
