If truth already gives a belief its epistemic value, why does adding reliability, justification, or another property give it additional value? ... some components may be derivationally or normatively parasitic on others. That resembles our anti-double-counting principle
a_rows_sample.statement: Draws an explicit structural analogy between the philosophical 'swamping problem' (does adding reliability/justification to an already-true belief add genuine additional value, or is it parasitic on truth) and the corpus's own kernel-minimality question (which capabilities are genuinely irreducible), warning against summing K=Truth+Evidence+Reliability+Justification+... without checking for derivational/normative parasitism, consistent with the existing anti-double-counting discipline.

a_rows_sample.anchor: we should not build KnowledgeOS around a single scalar Knowledge Quality ... V_epi(K) = (V_truth, V_just, V_reliability, V_understanding, V_explanatory, V_inquiry, ...) ... fits our previous rejection of scalar cancellation in Zero Algebra.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a candidate vector-valued epistemic-value assessment V_epi(K)=(V_truth,V_just,V_reliability,V_understanding,V_explanatory,V_inquiry,...) with dimensions left open, explicitly rejecting a single scalar Knowledge Quality, consistent with the corpus's prior rejection of scalar cancellation in Zero Algebra; also states False Model does not imply Zero Epistemic Value, and Useful Model does not imply Truth, extending the existing Model!=Truth, Fit!=Validity, Understanding!=Knowledge chain.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KR-EPISTEMIC-VALUE-LENS-2026-09 ... EV1 ... Is epistemic value distinct from epistemic correctness? ... EV10 ... Does epistemic value depend on context/purpose without making truth itself context-relative? ... Epistemic Success, Explanatory/Understanding Success, Practical/Action Success ... They can correlate. They can also diverge.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes KR-EPISTEMIC-VALUE-LENS-2026-09 with ten research questions EV1-EV10 (epistemic value vs correctness, knowledge vs understanding, explanatory structure representability, reliability-independent-of-truth value, non-scalar value, value-vs-inquiry-selection, value-vs-action-utility, process-attributable success, false/idealized models retaining value, context-dependent value without relativizing truth), concluding with the strongest preliminary hypothesis that KnowledgeOS eventually needs three distinguishable notions of success (Epistemic, Explanatory/Understanding, Practical/Action) that can correlate or diverge; explicitly [EXT]->[PROP]->[EXP]->[NEG] only, no promotion into Theory v1.2.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Epistemic Outcome != Epistemic Process ... Value(State) and Value(Process) ... Same conclusion. Different epistemic achievement. ... Epistemic Success = Outcome Quality + Process Attribution. But that equation is not established. It is a research hypothesis.
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies the omission of Value(State) vs Value(Process) (Goldman/Olsson reliabilism): two findings with the identical conclusion ('GitLab Runner caused the egress') can differ in epistemic achievement depending on whether the process involved independent validated multi-hypothesis investigation or a single misleading log, giving Epistemic Outcome != Epistemic Process and the unestablished candidate hypothesis Epistemic Success = Outcome Quality + Process Attribution.

a_rows_sample.anchor: context of discovery ... context of the final product ... Value(E | Discovery) != Value(E | FinalState). ... A clue that is enormously valuable while searching can become redundant after determination.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extracts Kusch's context-of-discovery vs context-of-final-product distinction, proposing that evidence value can depend on the stage of inquiry, Value(E|Discovery) != Value(E|FinalState), so KnowledgeOS should not treat evidence as having a timeless scalar value -- directly relevant to Fact-Finding and Zoom-In.

a_rows_sample.anchor: knowledge as a collective good ... K_t^collective ... Is KnowledgeOS fundamentally an individual epistemic system, or a distributed/collective epistemic system?
a_rows_sample.statement: Extracts Kusch's social/collective account of knowledge (informant, inquirer, social institution of testimony) as motivating the open question whether KnowledgeOS is fundamentally an individual epistemic system or a distributed/collective one, proposing a candidate K_t^collective spanning agents, sources, testimony, validation, and shared state.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the concept of knowledge economically packages multiple valuable properties. He compares it to a Swiss Army knife ... Is KnowledgeOS a semantic compression/packaging mechanism? ... connects directly to our representation reduction research.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extracts Weiner's 'Swiss Army knife' analogy (knowledge is valuable because it economically packages multiple valuable properties rather than adding a mysterious extra value) as motivating the research hypothesis that KnowledgeOS's Knowledge State representation might function as a semantic compression/packaging mechanism (KnowledgeState=Package(Truth,Evidence,Standing,Provenance,Context,...)), connecting to the existing representation-reduction research and the Adequacy != Minimality != Q-equivalence distinction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: value pluralism ... the values need not themselves all be epistemic -- they can be pragmatic, moral, aesthetic, etc. ... context-relativity of value does not imply context-relativity of truth.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extracts Baehr's value-pluralism reframing (ask the full range of ways an epistemic state can be valuable, rather than whether knowledge scalarly exceeds true belief) to reject a premature additive V_epi(K)=V_truth+V_justification+V_understanding, proposing instead Value(K,Q,C,P)->V_possible with values potentially epistemic, pragmatic, moral, or aesthetic, while explicitly preserving that context-relativity of value does not imply context-relativity of truth.

a_rows_sample.anchor: epistemic judgments contain a special kind of 'should', a binding/reason-giving character, rather than merely a calculation of which belief best achieves some goal. ... Epistemic Norm != Utility Function ... Epistemic 'Should' != Practical 'Should'.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extracts Grimm's argument that epistemic normativity is not reducible to teleological goal-promotion, giving Epistemic Norm != Utility Function and Epistemic 'Should' != Practical 'Should', requiring KR-EXPECTED-UTILITY to remain downstream of epistemic assessment rather than silently defining epistemic rationality.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Which goods are actually capable of motivating belief? ... Reason to Believe != Reason to Investigate != Reason to Act.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extracts Jones's evidentialist/pragmatist question of which goods can motivate belief (as opposed to motivating action to acquire a belief), giving the three-way separation Reason to Believe != Reason to Investigate != Reason to Act, directly relevant to Epistemic Agency and Action Fact-Finding.

a_rows_sample.anchor: an ugly/complex analysis of a valuable concept does not show that the concept itself lacks value ... Complex formalization not-implies Bad epistemic architecture ... Elegant minimal formalization not-implies Correct epistemic theory ... semantic minimality != syntactic minimality.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extracts DePaul's 'ugly analysis' lesson (a complicated analysis of a valuable concept does not undermine the concept's value) as a methodological warning for kernel minimality: Complex formalization does not imply Bad epistemic architecture, and Elegant minimal formalization does not imply Correct epistemic theory, reinforcing semantic minimality != syntactic minimality -- the kernel must not be chosen merely because it is mathematically prettier.

a_rows_sample.anchor: understanding can be a relation to a comprehensive, coherent body of commitments ... Knowledge Element versus Understanding Structure. The latter is not just a larger set of Knowledge Elements. It is a relational organization.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extracts Kvanvig/Elgin's account of understanding as relational organization (not merely a larger set of propositions) to propose Knowledge Element vs Understanding Structure as a candidate distinction relevant to the Knowledge Graph research; and extracts Elgin's felicitous-falsehoods thesis (idealizations can support scientific understanding while remaining literally false, provided the theory stays answerable to evidence) to give Understanding != Factive Knowledge and False component does not imply the entire explanatory structure is worthless.

a_rows_sample.anchor: understanding involves not merely possessing information, but an ability to use it -- reason with it, apply it, generate hypotheses from it, and assess its limits. ... EpistemicCapability(K_t): What can the system actually do with what it knows?
a_rows_sample.statement: Extracts Elgin's ability-to-use dimension of understanding to propose EpistemicCapability(K_t) as distinct from KnowledgeState(K_t), asking what the system can actually do with what it knows, potentially important for the 60-capability catalogue work; also extracts Riggs's control/attribution anti-luck account giving Outcome != Epistemic Achievement (a correct answer by luck differs in epistemic status from a correct answer through controlled process) and a candidate 'degrees of understanding' UnderstandingProfile(Q) rather than a scalar.

a_rows_sample.anchor: value can be relational rather than intrinsic ... Value(K_t | Q,C,P,S) is a much more promising research object. ... seven research primitives ... EV-1 Epistemic Outcome ... EV-7 Social/Collective Epistemic Value ... this is a research map, not Theory v1.3.
a_rows_sample.statement: Consolidates the second-pass reading into seven candidate research primitives (EV-1 Epistemic Outcome, EV-2 Epistemic Process, EV-3 Epistemic Achievement, EV-4 Understanding Structure, EV-5 Epistemic Norm, EV-6 Value Relation, EV-7 Social/Collective Epistemic Value) and a revised value-as-relation formula Value(K_t|Q,C,P,S), presenting a research-map architecture (Epistemic State->Truth/Justification/Reliability->Determination->Knowledge/Understanding/Model->Epistemic Value->Inquiry/Social/Practical Value->Agency->Action) explicitly not Theory v1.3.

a_rows_sample.anchor: THE SEVEN EPISTEMIC RESEARCH PRIMITIVES ... EV-1: Epistemic Outcome ... EV-7: Collective Infrastructure ... KR-EPISTEMIC-ACHIEVEMENT-LENS-2026-09 ... EA1-EA14
a_rows_sample.statement: Maps the seven EV-1..EV-7 primitives to concrete KnowledgeOS system-mechanics interpretations and registers KR-EPISTEMIC-ACHIEVEMENT-LENS-2026-09 (status [EXT][PROP], prerequisite KR-ZOOM-FACTFINDING-01) with an expanded fourteen-question research ledger EA1-EA14 spanning process attribution, inquiry-stage value, collective infrastructure, packaging, value-as-relation, norm/utility decoupling, reason-type separation, and understanding representation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The book gives us distinctions and research questions; it does not give KnowledgeOS metrics, operators, or invariants. ... remove 'anti-luck score' ... The book gives us a philosophical problem ... It does not give us a KnowledgeOS scoring function.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the key governance principle for the whole Epistemic Value lens: the book gives distinctions and research questions, not KnowledgeOS metrics, operators, or invariants; on this basis removes EV-3's invented 'anti-luck score'/'ability control measure' since the source supports only the research question of process attribution, not a scoring function, and downgrades all seven primitives from implied artifacts to [EXT][PROP] research directions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EV-1 needs one correction ... F_t = Determination and K_t = Knowledge State. A determination can contribute to a state, but they are not the same object. ... F_t != K_t.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects EV-1's grouping of 'the static determination F_t, claim, or state K_t reached' (conflating two distinct objects) to F_t != K_t, redefining EV-1 as the epistemic result reached by an inquiry (a determination, assessment, commitment, or attributed epistemic state), strengthening rather than weakening the source's contribution to existing theory.

b_rows_sample.anchor: At every observation you have infinite possible dimensions to be discovered. ... the projection to different observation field by zooming in can be the fact finding process about an event or process
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes that at every observation there is a potentially unbounded discoverable dimension space, and that zooming into different observation fields to find causes/situations/sources of an event constitutes the fact-finding process about that event, using a Nexus egress=70GB/day example with potentially relevant dimensions {Network,Backup,Repository,CI/CD,GitLabRunner,Configuration,Users,Traffic,Logs,Storage,Time,Security,Deployment,...}.

b_rows_sample.anchor: D_t subseteq D* and potentially D* -> open/unbounded discovery space. ... Don't claim literally that the dimensions are mathematically infinite unless the model establishes such a domain. Instead: the discoverable dimension space is open-ended relative to the current representation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the informal 'infinite possible dimensions' claim to a precise formulation: the currently represented dimensions D_t are a subset of a potentially discoverable D*, and the discoverable dimension space is open-ended relative to the current representation (D_t -Inquiry-> D_{t+1}), without D_{t+1} necessarily being a superset of D_t since dimensions can also become irrelevant/superseded/out-of-contract.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ZoomIn(K_t,O,Q) -> FocusedInquirySpace ... The dimensions explored by Zoom-in need not have been present in the original observation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reformulates Zoom-in from the earlier K_t->Subgraph(K_t) (found inadequate) to ZoomIn(K_t,O,Q)->FocusedInquirySpace, where focus is not deletion of the rest of K_t and the explored dimensions need not have been present in the original observation -- a discovery operation rather than a within-representation detail operation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Graph Traversal != Epistemic Investigation ... KnowledgeGraph = representational substrate ... ZoomIn = inquiry-directed exploration over that substrate and its discoverable extensions.
b_rows_sample.statement: Separates Graph Traversal (a Knowledge Graph can represent an edge like GitLabRunner-causes->Egress) from Epistemic Investigation (KnowledgeOS asks why the edge should exist, requiring Evidence, Provenance, Time, AlternativeHypotheses, Assessment, Determination), giving KnowledgeGraph=representational substrate while ZoomIn=inquiry-directed exploration over that substrate and its discoverable extensions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ZoomOut(F_t,K_t) = Integrate(Finding,F_t,K_t) rather than simply FocusedState -> OriginalState. ... this is exactly why our previous Zoom-out experiments struggled: we were trying to classify Zoom-out before clearly separating restoration from integration.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reframes Zoom-out from mere restoration (FocusedState->OriginalState) to Integration: ZoomOut(F_t,K_t)=Integrate(Finding,F_t,K_t), diagnosing that prior Zoom-out experiments struggled because they attempted to classify Zoom-out before separating restoration from integration.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ZoomIn = search for potentially relevant structure ... Zero = test eliminability of represented structure. ... ZoomIn discovers and Zero tests.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes Zoom-in and Zero as complementary operations relative to the same (Q,C,Pi,S): Zoom-in searches for potentially relevant structure (discovers), Zero tests eliminability of represented structure (tests); a candidate pipeline ZoomIn->ExpandedRepresentation->ZeroLens->RelevantSubspace->FactFinding is proposed but explicitly not assumed to be a fixed order, tagged [PROP] not axiom.

b_rows_sample.anchor: projection to different observation field ... I would be careful. ... Unless we have pi^2=pi or an appropriate semantic projection definition, don't call every Zoom-in a projection. Use inquiry-relative view transformation ... or focus transformation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns against calling every Zoom-in operation a mathematical 'projection' unless an established idempotent projection structure (pi^2=pi) or semantic-projection definition is demonstrated; recommends 'inquiry-relative view transformation' or 'focus transformation' as neutral terminology, consistent with the Zero Algebra lesson to discover the algebra rather than impose it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ZoomIn: Where should I investigate? EpistemicAgency: What should I do next? FactFinding: What does the evidence establish? ZoomOut: How does the finding change the broader state?
b_rows_sample.statement: Separates four distinct research questions into a coherent architecture: ZoomIn (where should I investigate), Epistemic Agency (what should I do next), Fact Finding (what does the evidence establish), Zoom-out (how does the finding change the broader state), combined into Observation->Relevance->ZoomIn->DimensionDiscovery->FactFinding->Determination->ZoomOut->Integration->K_{t+1} with a feedback loop from DimensionDiscovery back to NewObservation->NewZoomIn.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KR-ZOOM-FACTFINDING-2026-09 ... ZF1 -- Context preservation ... ZF2 -- Dimension expansion ... ZF3 -- Cross-boundary discovery ... ZF4 -- Determination dependence ... ZF5 -- Investigation != determination ... ZF6 -- Zoom-out integration ... ZF7 -- Resource/agency interaction
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies KR-ZOOM-FACTFINDING-2026-09 with seven candidate hypotheses: ZF1 ZoomIn(K_t,Q) does not imply Delete(K_t); ZF2 D_t subseteq D_{t+1} can occur through investigation; ZF3 a relevant dimension need not be contained in the initial observation's representation; ZF4 newly discovered dimensions can change Determine(Q); ZF5 ZoomIn != Determine; ZF6 a finding discovered during Zoom-in can modify the broader state; ZF7 the next investigated dimension depends on K,Q,Delta,Resources,Context,Contract,Risk.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Backup -> large transfer, GitLab Runner -> large transfer, Replication -> large transfer ... the system must not say I found GitLab Runner, therefore GitLab Runner is the cause. ... No Determination Without Alternative Space.
b_rows_sample.statement: Uses a multi-cause Nexus-egress failure case (Backup, GitLab Runner, and Replication all plausibly producing large transfer) to argue against single-hypothesis-collapse ('I found X, therefore X is the cause'), requiring the full hypothesis set H_Q to undergo Evidence Assessment before Determination, stated as the principle 'No Determination Without Alternative Space.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: O_t -> ZoomIn(K_t,O_t,Q) -> D_t subseteq D_{t+1} -> Acquire -> Assess -> Determine -> ZoomOut(Finding,K_t) -> K_{t+1} ... Terminology Correction: View Transformation vs. Projection
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes a four-level Decoupled Dimensional Expansion & Integration Pipeline (1. Observation Entry O_t={d_0}; 2. Dimensional Discovery ZoomIn(K_t,O_t,Q)->D_t subseteq D_{t+1}; 3. Fact-Finding Acquire->Assess->Determine; 4. Integration ZoomOut(Finding,K_t)->K_{t+1}), and replaces the term 'projection' with 'Inquiry-Directed View Transformation' to avoid assuming idempotence (pi^2=pi) prior to empirical discovery.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t <=_O Focus(K_t,Q) where <=_O means that the focused view does not make previously available contract-relevant observations unavailable. ... ZF1 -- Context Preservation: Zoom-In changes inquiry focus without itself removing or invalidating surrounding Knowledge State.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects ZF1's undefined comparison ZoomIn(K_t,Q)!=Delete(K_t) to K_t<=_O Focus(K_t,Q), where <=_O means the focused view does not make previously available contract-relevant observations unavailable, avoiding accidentally turning Zoom-In into an undefined representation-theoretic operation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Discovery of a dimension != acceptance of that dimension into Knowledge State. ... exactly analogous to your existing Candidate != Determined != Knowledge. ... ZF2 -- Dimensional Expansion: Inquiry-directed investigation can introduce candidate explanatory dimensions not represented in the initial active representation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects ZF2's D_t subset D_{t+1} (which conflates dimension discovery with state evolution) by introducing D_t^cand as candidate dimensional space distinct from D_t^rep (accepted into Knowledge State), giving D_t^rep subseteq D_{t+1}^cand and a later integration D_{t+1}^cand -> D_{t+1}^rep, analogous to the existing Candidate != Determined != Knowledge chain.

b_rows_sample.anchor: d* not-in Rep_active(O_t,K_t) AND d* in Discover(I_t) ... ZF3 currently risks becoming tautological ... GitLab Runner may already exist somewhere in the Knowledge Graph but not be connected to the egress observation. That is not dimensional discovery.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects ZF3's under-specified d* not-in Rep(O_t) (risking tautology) by distinguishing not-observable-in-O_t, not-represented-in-K_t, and genuinely-discovered-during-investigation, requiring d* not-in Rep_active(O_t,K_t) AND d* in Discover(investigation trace I_t), noting a dimension already present elsewhere in the graph but unconnected to the observation does not count as dimensional discovery.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Determine(K_t,Q,C,E_C,S,R) != Determine(K'_t,Q,C,E_C,S,R) with K'_t = Expand(K_t,d*). ... Otherwise a change in determination could simply result from changing standards, evidence, inquiry, or reasoning regime.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects ZF4 (Determine(Q|D_t)!=Determine(Q|D')) to hold the full determination signature Q,C,EC,S,R fixed and intervene only on the discovered dimensional representation, giving Determine(K_t,...)!=Determine(K'_t,...) with K'_t=Expand(K_t,d*), so the change is attributable to dimensional expansion alone rather than confounded with standards/evidence/inquiry/reasoning-regime changes.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A Zoom-In that discovers ... has succeeded even if Fact-Finding concludes: Cause remains underdetermined. So: DiscoverySuccess not-implies Determination should probably become a candidate invariant.
b_rows_sample.statement: Retains and operationally sharpens ZF5 (ZoomIn:(K_t,O_t,Q)->D^cand versus FactFinding:(D^cand,E,H_Q,M,S)->Standing->Determination), proposing the candidate invariant DiscoverySuccess does not imply Determination: Zoom-In can succeed in surfacing candidates even when Fact-Finding concludes the cause remains underdetermined.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ZoomOut should not be defined as ZoomOut(ZoomIn(K_t))=K_t. That would recreate the old restoration model. Instead: ZoomOut(F,K_t) = Integrate(K_t,F) -> K_{t+1} ... ZoomOut = integration of finding rather than: ZoomOut = inverse(ZoomIn).
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly forbids defining Zoom-Out as the inverse of Zoom-In (ZoomOut(ZoomIn(K_t))=K_t would recreate the old restoration model); Zoom-Out is Integrate(K_t,F)->K_{t+1} where F may contain newly discovered dimensions, assessed evidence, determined relationships, rejected hypotheses, unresolved alternatives, provenance, and temporal information, so K_{t+1}!=K_t may occur even though Zoom-In itself deleted nothing.

b_rows_sample.anchor: d* in ArgMax_{d in D^cand} E[V_Delta(d|K,Q,C,S,R)]/Cost(d) as a candidate agency policy, not a kernel law. ... ZoomIn != Agency. Agency selects the next investigation; Zoom-In executes the inquiry-directed focus.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects ZF7's dimension-selection formula (which assumed Adeq is measurable, candidate dimensions are comparably valued, costs are scalarizable, and an argmax exists) to an explicitly candidate agency policy d* in ArgMax_{d}E[V_Delta(d|K,Q,C,S,R)]/Cost(d), not a kernel law, reaffirming ZoomIn != Agency (Agency selects the next investigation, Zoom-In executes the inquiry-directed focus).

b_rows_sample.anchor: ZF8 -- Representation Boundary Non-Closure ... An initial observation representation must not be assumed to contain all relevant explanatory dimensions. ... ZF3 asks: Can the relevant dimension cross the initial boundary? ZF8 asks: Is the initial dimensional representation itself epistemically non-closed?
b_rows_sample.statement: Adds ZF8 (Representation Boundary Non-Closure): the initial observation representation must not be assumed to contain all relevant explanatory dimensions, distinguished from ZF3 (can a relevant dimension cross the boundary) by asking instead whether the initial representation is itself epistemically non-closed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zoom-In != Zero != Fact-Finding ... Determination ... Zoom-Out ... Epistemic Agency ... This is much more promising than trying to make Zoom-In or Zoom-Out kernel primitives.
b_rows_sample.statement: States a six-way functional separation as the architectural conclusion: Zoom-In (expand/search the inquiry space) != Zero Lens (determine what can be eliminated while preserving contract) != Fact-Finding (establish what evidence supports) != Determination (establish what can be decided under the epistemic regime) != Zoom-Out (integrate finding into broader state) != Epistemic Agency (select what to investigate/do next); recommends testing ZF2+ZF3+ZF5 first as the foundational experiment before the rest of the architecture is tested.

a_notations: Epistemic State != Epistemic Quality != Epistemic Value != Practical Value
a_aliases: Epistemic Value (ed. Haddock, Millar, Pritchard) as a KnowledgeOS research lens
b_aliases: Zoom-in as fact-finding discovery, not detail-inspection

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels co-occur in the same contribution's labels[] 3 separate times across the corpus

a_rows_sample.anchor: We now move from theoretical composition to experimental falsification. If a concept cannot ultimately be represented and computed, it is not yet a sufficiently defined part of the KnowledgeOS model. We therefore build a minimal executable reference model, not the production system. The purpose is n
a_rows_sample.statement: Announces the shift from theoretical composition to experimental falsification: a minimal executable reference model (not production code) whose purpose is to discover contradictions, undefined transitions, hidden assumptions, and non-computable definitions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Objective of Step 25 ... Can the complete KnowledgeOS model execute end-to-end on finite data? X=\{Documents,Databases,InternetArtifacts,Rules,Constitution,ADRs,Instructions,AIOutputs,Textbooks,Settings,Manifestos\}, can we transform it into a governed knowledge state X\rightarrow K and then execute
a_rows_sample.statement: States the Step 25 objective: can the complete model execute end-to-end on finite data, transforming an eleven-kind heterogeneous input set X into a governed K and running the full operational loop.

a_rows_sample.anchor: If the reference model cannot represent a case, the theory has a hole. If it can represent it but cannot compute the required result, the operator is incomplete. If it computes an incorrect result, our semantics or invariant is wrong.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the three-way diagnostic logic for the reference model: unrepresentable case = theoretical hole; representable-but-uncomputable = incomplete operator; wrong result = wrong semantics/invariant.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The experimental universe ... Entities E_1=KnowledgeOS, E_2=Nexus, E_3=NexusHost, E_4=Repository, E_5=ArchitectureBoard. ... World state S_0 ... Version(Nexus)=3.69 ... Repositories(Nexus)=43 ... BlobStores(Nexus)=40. ... Evidence inputs ... e_1 Infrastructure inventory ... e_6 LLM-generated extract
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies the small artificial enterprise world: five entities, a world state S_0 with four concrete Nexus facts, and six heterogeneous evidence items e1-e6 each carrying Source/Timestamp/Origin/Content/Provenance.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Deliberate contradiction ... e_1: Version=3.69 and e_2: Version=3.72. We do not tell the system which is correct. The expected result is Conflict(Version) not Version=3.72 simply because e_2 appeared later.
a_rows_sample.statement: Designs a deliberate-contradiction test: two evidence items disagree on version, with the expected result being an explicit Conflict marker, never silently preferring the later-arriving value.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Deliberate stale evidence ... e_3: Version=3.69 with Timestamp=t_0. Then current time t_1\gg t_0. The assertion may still be historically valid. Therefore the system must distinguish HistoricalTruth from CurrentTruth. Expected: ValidAt(e,t_0)=True while CurrentAt(e,t_1) may be unknown.
a_rows_sample.statement: Designs a stale-evidence test distinguishing HistoricalTruth from CurrentTruth: an old timestamped assertion remains ValidAt(t0)=True while CurrentAt(t1) is Unknown.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Deliberate identity ambiguity ... Reference A: nexus3.dgverlag.de ... Reference B: 10.61.133.85 ... Reference C: "Nexus server". The system must determine Identity(A,B,C). But we deliberately make one mapping ambiguous. Expected: IdentityStatus=Ambiguous rather than forced resolution.
a_rows_sample.statement: Designs an identity-ambiguity test across three references, expecting IdentityStatus=Ambiguous rather than a forced resolution.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Deliberate duplicate evidence ... e_4=e_5. Register(e_4) followed by Register(e_5). Expected behavior: No semantic duplication. This tests idempotency.
a_rows_sample.statement: Designs a duplicate-registration idempotency test: registering the same evidence twice must produce no semantic duplication.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Deliberate LLM output ... The Nexus server has sufficient backup capability for migration. But no underlying source supports that claim. KnowledgeOS must represent CandidateAssertion. It must not automatically create CommittedKnowledge. This tests one of our strongest AI boundaries.
a_rows_sample.statement: Designs an unsupported-LLM-claim test: an assertion with no underlying source must remain CandidateAssertion, never CommittedKnowledge — one of the strongest AI boundaries.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Deliberate unsupported certainty ... Input: "Backup appears to exist." LLM: "Backup is definitely valid." Expected: Confidence_{output} cannot exceed what the transformation justifies. This tests our NoFalsePrecision invariant.
a_rows_sample.statement: Designs a NoFalsePrecision test: an LLM's overconfident restatement ('definitely valid') of a hedged input ('appears to exist') must not be allowed to exceed the justified confidence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Rules and constitution ... R_1: Production changes require authorization ... R_2: HighRiskMigration requires rollback capability. These are not empirical evidence. They originate from Constitution/Policy. This tests whether the architecture correctly distinguishes NormativeKnowledge from EmpiricalKn
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces three normative-knowledge test inputs (constitution rules, an ADR, a human instruction) testing NormativeKnowledge vs EmpiricalKnowledge separation, ADR scope/validity evaluation, and Instruction vs Evidence separation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The first complete knowledge state ... K_0 might contain Entities, Assertions, Evidence, Rules, Constraints, ADRs, Conflicts, Unknowns, Provenance, Temporal validity, Identity mappings. Importantly, K_0 contains both what is currently established and what remains unresolved.
a_rows_sample.statement: Constructs the expected K_0 structure after ingesting all the above test inputs, containing eleven categories including both established facts and unresolved items.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Test Zero ... G="Prepare Nexus for governed migration." I={SupportedVersion,BackupVerified,RollbackVerified,TargetReady,AuthorizationAvailable}. Zero computes \Delta(K_0,G,I). Expected: Known: Current version. Missing: Backup verification, Rollback verification, Target readiness, Authorization.
a_rows_sample.statement: Designs a Zero(K0,G,I) test expected to find one known item (current version) and four missing requirements.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Test the epistemic contract ... EC_{migration} ... R=\{CurrentVersion,TargetVersion,Backup,Rollback,Dependencies,Authorization\}. Then calculate Sat(K_0,R_i). We expect ReadyForExecution=False. This must be a deterministic result under the defined contract.
a_rows_sample.statement: Designs a deterministic ReadyForExecution=False test against a six-requirement migration epistemic contract.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Test Lord ... Lord receives \Delta. It should generate candidate information actions: a_1=VerifyBackup, a_2=TestRollback, a_3=InspectTargetEnvironment. These are not yet migration actions. They are EpistemicActions.

Then Outcome_1 \rightarrow Observation \rightarrow Evidence \rightarrow K_1. Now Sat(K_1,Backup)=True. ... Second iteration ... Zero recalculates \Delta(K_1,G,I). The b
a_rows_sample.statement: Runs the designed VerifyBackup action through Outcome→Observation→Evidence→K1, testing incremental gap closure (backup gap closes, rollback gap remains) rather than a premature readiness declaration.

This is important. The knowledge state became worse for the purpose even though we acquired more information. That proves MoreKnowled

a_rows_sample.statement: Designs a governance-boundary test: without approval, execution must fail at the governance layer (a key safety property); only after an ApprovalEvent may execution begin.

S \rightarrow Observation \rightarrow E \rightarrow K \rightarrow Decision \rightarrow A \rightarrow S' followed by S' \rightarrow Observation \rightarrow E' \rightarrow K'. This gives us a

Reasoning: K\rightarrow DerivedKnowledge ... Zero: (K,I)\rightarrow \Delta ... Lord: (\Delta,G,K)\rightarrow\mathcal A ... Sārath
b_rows_sample.statement: Verifies type consistency by chaining all ten major transformations' input/output types end to end, noting any undefined type boundary would fail the model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Type closure ... \forall x\in Domain(f),\quad f(x)\in Y. ... an LLM cannot directly produce CommittedKnowledge unless the commitment boundary explicitly permits it. LLMOutput \not\rightarrow CommittedKnowledge by default. Instead LLMOutput \rightarrow CandidateAssertion \rightarrow Assessment \right
b_rows_sample.statement: States the type-closure requirement ∀x∈Domain(f), f(x)∈Y, applied to forbid LLMOutput→CommittedKnowledge by default, requiring the full CandidateAssertion→Assessment→Commitment path.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Composition ... Observation \rightarrow Evidence \rightarrow Knowledge. And Knowledge \rightarrow Discrepancy \rightarrow Action. And Action \rightarrow Outcome \rightarrow Evidence.
b_rows_sample.statement: Verifies functions compose as expected across the three major sub-chains (Observation→Evidence→Knowledge; Knowledge→Discrepancy→Action; Action→Outcome→Evidence).

b_rows_sample.anchor: The critical circularity ... Knowledge \rightarrow Action \rightarrow Outcome \rightarrow Knowledge. Is this a mathematical contradiction? No. It is a state transition loop. K_t \xrightarrow{Action} S_{t+1} \xrightarrow{Observation} K_{t+1}. The time index prevents the circularity from becoming an a
b_rows_sample.statement: Resolves the apparent Knowledge→Action→Outcome→Knowledge circularity: it is a temporally-indexed state transition loop (K_t→K_{t+1}), not an algebraic self-reference (K_t→K_t) — no contradiction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Temporal closure ... Knowledge Update must be temporally ordered. If an event occurs at t_1 and is observed at t_2>t_1, then K_{t_2} may incorporate that observation. It must not silently modify K_{t_0} for t_0<t_1. ... Historical knowledge ... K_t=T(K_0,e_1,\ldots,e_t). This is one of the most impo
b_rows_sample.statement: States Knowledge Update must be temporally ordered — a later observation may update K_{t2} but must never silently modify an earlier K_{t0} — requiring historical reconstructibility K_t=T(K_0,e_1,...,e_t).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Identity consistency ... Identity(E,t_1)=Identity(E,t_2) unless there is an explicit identity transition. StateChange\neq IdentityChange. ... Identity contradiction ... FQDN\rightarrow E_1 and FQDN\rightarrow E_2. KnowledgeOS must not silently choose one. It must create IdentityConflict.
b_rows_sample.statement: States Identity(E,t1)=Identity(E,t2) absent an explicit identity transition (StateChange≠IdentityChange), and requires an explicit IdentityConflict object rather than silently choosing between contradictory identity claims.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence conservation ... E\rightarrow A, the conclusion must retain a reference to E. DerivedKnowledge \Rightarrow TraceableEvidence. We should never have "KnowledgeOS believes X" without being able to determine why. ... Evidence conservation does not mean every conclusion needs raw evidence ... A_
b_rows_sample.statement: States DerivedKnowledge⇒TraceableEvidence — every conclusion must reference its evidence, and lineage chains must eventually terminate in provenance-bearing inputs (or explicit axioms/normative premises).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Axioms are special ... x+y=y+x within a mathematical structure. Or an organizational constitution may establish: Production changes require approval. OriginType\in\{Observation,Normative,Axiom,Definition,Derived,HumanDecision\}. This prevents us from forcing all knowledge into empirical evidence.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a six-value OriginType enum {Observation,Normative,Axiom,Definition,Derived,HumanDecision}, explicitly preventing forcing all knowledge into empirical evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Uncertainty preservation ... x\in[10,20]. A transformation must not silently produce x=15. unless there is a valid inference rule. Transformation must preserve epistemic information. ... False precision ... No transformation may increase precision without justification. Date\approx August cannot bec
b_rows_sample.statement: States transformations must preserve epistemic information — no unjustified precision increase, illustrated by an interval [10,20] that must not silently become a point value, and an approximate date that must not become exact merely from an LLM guess.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Uncertainty monotonicity ... KnowledgeOS does not require uncertainty to monotonically decrease. New evidence can increase uncertainty. Initially A appears certain. New evidence reveals A\lor B. The epistemic state becomes more uncertain. Knowledge acquisition need not monotonically reduce uncertain
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects any assumption of monotonic uncertainty reduction or knowledge growth: new evidence can increase uncertainty, and a committed assertion can later be retracted (A∈K_t, A∉K_{t+1}) — this is epistemic revision, not inconsistency.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Belief revision ... Revision as a first-class operation. Revise(K,E_{new}) \rightarrow K'. The revision must preserve reason; evidence; temporal position; affected dependencies.
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires Revision be a first-class operation Revise(K,E_new)→K' preserving reason, evidence, temporal position, and affected dependencies.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Dependency consistency ... If A is retracted, KnowledgeOS must determine whether B remains valid. Retracting a premise triggers dependency analysis. It does not necessarily automatically invalidate every descendant. ... Why not automatically delete descendants? ... If A is retracted but C independen
b_rows_sample.statement: States retracting a premise triggers dependency analysis (not automatic deletion) — a descendant supported by an independent second premise may survive retraction of one, requiring re-evaluation not blind deletion.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Provenance closure ... Every committed assertion should be traceable to origin; transformation; assessor; authority; time; policy. Provenance(CommittedKnowledge)\neq\varnothing for governed knowledge.
b_rows_sample.statement: States Provenance(CommittedKnowledge)≠∅ — every committed assertion must be traceable to origin, transformation, assessor, authority, time, and policy.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Governance closure ... Action \Rightarrow Authorization for governed actions. If Authorization=Unknown, the system must not convert it to Authorized=True. ... Safety invariant ... UnknownAuthorization \not\Rightarrow Authorization. And RejectedAuthorization \Rightarrow NoExecution. This is a critica
b_rows_sample.statement: States governed actions require authorization; UnknownAuthorization must never become Authorization, and RejectedAuthorization must always block execution — a critical safety boundary.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Decision consistency ... D_t=f(K_t,\Pi_t). If later K_{t+1} changes, that does not mean D_t was irrational. It means the information state changed. ... Decision invalidation ... if A\in Dependencies(D), then Change(A) should trigger Review(D). KnowledgeChange \rightarrow PotentialDecisionReview.
b_rows_sample.statement: States a later knowledge change does not retroactively make an earlier decision irrational (D_t=f(K_t,Π_t) evaluated at its own time), but a change to a decision's dependency should trigger PotentialDecisionReview.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Idempotency ... Process(E) and again Process(E). We do not want duplicate knowledge artifacts. f(f(x))=f(x) where semantically appropriate. RegisterEvidence(E) should be idempotent based on evidence identity. ... Not every operation is idempotent ... IncrementCounter is not idempotent. Likewise Depl
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires operations like RegisterEvidence be idempotent (f(f(x))=f(x)) based on evidence identity, while others (IncrementCounter, Deploy) are not — idempotency is operation-specific and must be explicitly declared.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Determinism ... Hash(x) or ValidateSchema(x). Given identical inputs f(x)=f(x). Other processes may be nondeterministic, especially LLM generation. Determinism must be explicit per operation. ... LLM nondeterminism ... CandidateAssertion_1 on one execution and CandidateAssertion_2 on another. This d
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires determinism be declared explicitly per operation, with LLM nondeterminism confined to a CandidateGeneration boundary, followed by deterministic assessment where possible.

b_rows_sample.statement: The feedback-loop finding is formalized into a standing methodological constraint: before treating any Step-236-onward statement as independent evidence, fingerprint it, determine possible verifier-output origin, and classify it as INDEPENDENT CORPUS EVIDENCE / CORPUS RESPONSE TO VERIFICATION / UNKNOWN DEPENDENCE -- never counting an echoed verifier finding as independent corroboration; the loop is not to be retrospectively eliminated but maintained as two explicitly separate, never-silently-merged streams (Stream A historical/corpus evidence, Stream B verifier-derived findings).

b_rows_sample.anchor: C-4/C-7: ADDRESSED BUT NOT CLOSED ... DV-1 — the one unsafe-direction gap ... the durable copy is written twice after its last all-or-nothing verification ... and re-verified nowhere.
b_rows_sample.statement: AMD6's independent review finds a genuine safety gap (DV-1) in the durability migration plan: the durable authoritative copy is written after its last all-or-nothing verification and never re-verified before the source is removed, so Phase 7's gate could report success while the durable copy is silently incomplete.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 'the FIRST record in the authoritative store' is false under the plan's own record vocabulary ... Truth is 'first governance append after the writer switch'
b_rows_sample.statement: Names DV-3: the migration plan's acceptance criterion 17 uses an inaccurate phrase ('first record in the authoritative store', which is literally false because Phase 3 already copied records into it) and must be replaced by 'first governance append after the authority transfer.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Phase 5 remains prohibited ... DV-1 is the critical one because it creates an unsafe path to Phase 7.
b_rows_sample.statement: Prescribes the next lawful sequence after the DV-1..DV-7 findings: register/route a new Architecture correction commission only (not a Governance decision document), then Architecture authors the fix, then a fresh independent Architecture review, then Governance's bounded review, then PO/ARB; Phase 5 must not execute until DV-1 is repaired and reviewed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The durability migration chain (AMD3→AMD6) is literally the test corpus the assurance checker is being built to back-test against, and the checker's job list is literally the migration's own mandated pre-delivery verification.
b_rows_sample.statement: Finds that the two seemingly separate work items (cost-optimization/deterministic-assurance, and the durability migration) already share the same evidence base and back-test corpus, so integration is a sequencing/authority problem rather than a new architecture problem; the checker must remain warn-only through Phase 1 to avoid itself becoming a governance object requiring authority.

b_rows_sample.anchor: DV-1 = UNSAFE ... Business: Migration must not start yet because there is still a real risk of losing governance evidence.' Not: Migration is almost finished.
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked counterexample showing what an incorrect over-simplified business translation would say versus the correct uncertainty-preserving translation of the DV-1 durability finding.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Decision status is graded, not monolithic: ADR artifact = PROPOSED ('recommends an architecture and decides nothing'); a separate PO/ARB DECISION ACT (2026-08-19) = DECIDED: D1 = B′ adopted, D2 = R-CONFLICT adopt, D3 = existing placement governance.
b_rows_sample.statement: Establishes that decision status must be read as a graded record: an ADR document being PROPOSED does not contradict a separate PO/ARB decision act having already DECIDED specific numbered items from it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: D9 | Separation: source of execution vs evidence of execution vs authoritative decision record (B′ relocation, R-CONFLICT) | DECIDED (PO/ARB 2026-08-19, D1–D2) — recorded, not re-decided here
b_rows_sample.statement: Reconciliation-document claim register entry D9: the three-way separation and B′/R-CONFLICT decisions are recorded here as already DECIDED by a separate PO/ARB act, never re-decided by this reconciliation document itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 1 RE-HASH ... 1b RECONCILE/DISPOSE DELTA ... 2 READERS ... 3 THE WRITER ← THE AUTHORITY-TRANSFER INSTANT ... 4 RUNTIME DEMOTION MARKER ... 5 STAGING MARKER RETRACTION
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the single canonical Phase-5 slot sequence (1, 1b, 2, 3, 4, 5) with slot 1b's three outcomes (no delta/continue, reconcilable delta/continue, unreconcilable delta/freeze-violation-STOP), replacing two previously-competing enumerations.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A MOVE is refused because it would LAUNDER THE QUARANTINE — a post-demotion record lies OUTSIDE the enumeration by definition, so moving it out HIDES the quarantined evidence, makes the source SPURIOUSLY SATISFY criterion 12.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects an earlier, inverted justification for forbidding a quarantined record's relocation (previously reasoned as 'would alter the demoted store'); the true reason is that moving it would make a failing Phase-7 comparison spuriously pass.

b_rows_sample.anchor: OPEN-M7 — quarantine disposition — the disposer AND the path ... The one open item that can block the migration's COMPLETION indefinitely.
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies that the workflow mechanism has an act class for disposing a quarantine (a governance act) but literally no DISPOSE transition type, so an undisposed quarantine can block migration completion indefinitely by design, not by oversight.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A quarantine is a DOMAIN STATE with a business consequence, not a directory condition. The block is not a tooling limitation to engineer away — it is the aggregate refusing an invalid transition.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reframes quarantine-blocking-completion as a DDD invariant (an aggregate refusing an invalid state transition) rather than a filesystem/tooling limitation to be worked around.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the switch-over record is the FIRST GOVERNANCE APPEND AFTER THE AUTHORITY TRANSFER (⛔ superseded wording: 'that store's first record' — false, not merely imprecise: Phase 3 has already copied governance records into that store.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the acceptance-criterion phrase describing the authoritative store's identifying record: it must read 'first governance append after the authority transfer', not 'that store's first record', because prior copied records already exist there.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the grant count moved 110 → 114 since AMD5, and it is C-4's premise observed live: those four grants are AMD6's OWN commission, appended by P-1 into the corpus the migration freezes and hashes.
b_rows_sample.statement: A self-referential observation: the ongoing governance work authorizing this very amendment is itself appended to the corpus the migration plan proposes to freeze, meaning a literal freeze would have had to prohibit the act that authorized the amendment.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ELIGIBILITY OUTCOME AS RECORDED: bc1b47ef - AUTHORING ELIGIBLE, REVIEWING BARRED, ACCEPTING BARRED ... A FRESH INDEPENDENT ARCHITECTURE PROCESS - REVIEWING ... REQUIRED.
b_rows_sample.statement: A registered grant explicitly restores a producer's authoring eligibility while permanently barring it from reviewing or accepting its own amendment (AMD6), which the reviewer here reads directly from the record rather than inferring.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A reviewer checking only the two names it was handed would have PASSED this gate and proceeded ... this is exactly why the same commission forbids hand-copied grant lists: the chat-supplied exclusion set was narrower than the governed one.
b_rows_sample.statement: Demonstrates the failure mode of trusting a prompt-supplied exclusion list rather than the governed record: the chat-supplied set of two barred names missed a fourth clause that fires on a registered grant covering the same performer under a different role in this same chain.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 1 PO/ARB starts a FRESH Architecture session ... 2 that session DECLARES its own identity ... 3 GOVERNANCE ... appends REGISTER ... then HANDOFF ... 4 START recorded with THIS PO/ARB act as its humanAct ... 5 the fresh reviewer consumes G-…-DV-CORRECTION-READING-ORDER as its index
b_rows_sample.statement: Prescribes the exact five-step lawful sequence that would unblock the deadlocked reviewer-appointment problem without a barred process appointing its own judge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: THE REVIEWER MUST BE A FRESH INDEPENDENT ARCHITECTURE PROCESS ... Satisfied on the measurement in §2.2: this is a process with no registered role in the chain.
b_rows_sample.statement: Demonstrates the independence-verification method in practice: enumerate every process occurrence across all transitions and grants in the aggregate plus a whole-repository grep, and treat zero occurrences as the only admissible basis for eligibility.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the reviewer must not be its own registrar — the same reason bc1b47ef refused to appoint its own judge, applied to the other end of the same edge.
b_rows_sample.statement: Extends the 'a barred process must not appoint its own judge' principle to its symmetric case: an eligible candidate reviewer must also not register/hand-off its own assignment, since separation is the entire point of the lane.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the eligibility set keeps narrowing — every candidate reviewer that declares eligibility and is then not started adds one more name to it.
b_rows_sample.statement: Observes a structural risk pattern: repeatedly declaring and abandoning candidate reviewers without recording a START permanently shrinks the pool of processes still eligible to review, since each attempt itself becomes a disqualifying prior-participation fact.

b_rows_sample.anchor: independence is not transferable: an assignment whose recorded evidence names a8ce5a39 cannot be discharged by 8a525719 without the record asserting something false about who did the work.
b_rows_sample.statement: Names a second-order independence failure distinct from personal ineligibility: a genuinely independent process cannot discharge a review under a workflow lane whose registered execution context names a different process, since INV-ATTR-1 means the engine itself would never detect the substitution.

One important limitation mus
a_rows_sample.statement: Adopts an eight-value epistemic-status tagging scheme (established/proposed/assumed/experimental/rejected/unresolved/contradictory/missing) as the governing method for this handover, explicitly disclosing the extraction is a best-effort reconstruction, not a lossless transcript, with gaps marked rather than silently repaired.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Handover point: Step 25A.1 Next objective: Minimal Formal State and Type System Method: Senior Mathematics + Statistics + Principal Architecture + DDD Mode: Experimental falsification, not conceptual expansion.
a_rows_sample.statement: Positions this document as the handover point at Step 25A.1, with the next objective being the Minimal Formal State and Type System, explicitly in Experimental falsification mode, not conceptual expansion.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The central methodological principle is now: If an important concept cannot ultimately be represented and computed, its definition is not yet sufficiently mature. This does not mean every real-world problem must be algorithmically decidable. The model must instead distinguish deterministic computati
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates the central methodological principle (unrepresentable/uncomputable concepts are immature) and a seven-way computability classification.

a_rows_sample.anchor: [ESTABLISHED] The model evolved from an AI/knowledge architecture toward an explicit epistemic model. The important transition was from "How does an AI obtain information?" to "What constitutes knowledge, how is it justified, how does it change, and when is it sufficient for a purpose?"
a_rows_sample.statement: Marks [ESTABLISHED] the conceptual transition from an AI-information-acquisition framing to an explicit epistemic-justification-and-sufficiency framing.

a_rows_sample.anchor: [ESTABLISHED] The most important distinction is: WorldState \neq KnowledgeState. S_t\neq K_t. KnowledgeOS therefore does not possess reality. It possesses a time-dependent reconstruction/representation of what it can establish about reality.
a_rows_sample.statement: Marks [ESTABLISHED] the WorldState≠KnowledgeState distinction as the single most important result of the prior phase.

a_rows_sample.anchor: [ESTABLISHED / PROVISIONAL] K_{t+1} = T_K(K_t,E_{new},Rules,Context). Historical reconstruction was also expressed conceptually as K_t=Fold(K_0,e_1,\ldots,e_t). [ESTABLISHED] Knowledge is not necessarily monotonic. New evidence may add knowledge; invalidate knowledge; increase uncertainty; reveal co
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates the knowledge-evolution transition function and fold-based historical reconstruction as [ESTABLISHED/PROVISIONAL], and non-monotonic knowledge evolution (K_t⊆K_{t+1} is not a universal invariant) as [ESTABLISHED].

a_rows_sample.anchor: [ESTABLISHED] Historical knowledge must remain reconstructable. If a decision was made at t_0, then later information at t_1>t_0 must not silently alter the epistemic basis of the historical decision. Therefore Decision_{t_0} must reference the appropriate K_{t_0}. This is a critical protection agai
a_rows_sample.statement: Reaffirms [ESTABLISHED] the hindsight-contamination protection: historical decisions must reference their actual historical knowledge snapshot.

a_rows_sample.anchor: [ESTABLISHED] Source \rightarrow Artifact \rightarrow Observation \rightarrow Evidence \rightarrow Assessment \rightarrow Assertion \rightarrow Knowledge. These concepts must not be collapsed. Source Origin of information. Artifact Concrete information-bearing object. Observation Something observed/
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates the seven-stage evidence pipeline with brief definitions of each stage as [ESTABLISHED], explicitly flagging [UNRESOLVED] the exact mathematical predicates for Observation→Evidence and Assertion→CommittedKnowledge as central to future experiments.

a_rows_sample.anchor: [ESTABLISHED] KnowledgeState must accommodate assertions; uncertainty; conflict; temporal validity; revision; historical versions; provenance/lineage. [UNRESOLVED] The exact mathematical representation is not yet frozen. Questions that must be answered in Step 25A.1: Is K a set of assertions? Is it
a_rows_sample.statement: Flags KnowledgeState's exact mathematical representation as the critical open area, listing ten specific unanswered design questions to be resolved in Step 25A.1 rather than guessed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: [ESTABLISHED] The model explicitly distinguishes uncertainty; confidence; probability; evidence strength; reliability; sufficiency. A high confidence value does not imply that a decision is ready. Likewise, additional information can make an assessment less certain. [PROPOSED] Bayesian updating was
a_rows_sample.statement: Tags the uncertainty/confidence/probability separation as [ESTABLISHED], Bayesian updating as merely [PROPOSED] (not the universal mechanism), and lists seven [UNRESOLVED] statistical questions for the backlog.

a_rows_sample.anchor: [ESTABLISHED] The model explicitly rejects TemporalBefore\Rightarrow CausedBy. [PROPOSED] The model may eventually use P(Y\mid do(X=x)) and causal graphs. [UNRESOLVED] Full causal semantics belong to the later causal-reasoning stage. Step 25A should therefore be capable of representing causal hypoth
a_rows_sample.statement: Reaffirms TemporalBefore⇏CausedBy as [ESTABLISHED], do-calculus/causal graphs as merely [PROPOSED], deferring full causal semantics while requiring the ability to represent causal hypotheses.

a_rows_sample.anchor: [ESTABLISHED] Zero(K,G,I)\rightarrow\Delta ... Zero therefore cannot meaningfully operate on K alone. [UNRESOLVED] The exact mathematical structure of \Delta remains open. It might involve unresolved requirements; state differences; graph differences; constraint violations; uncertainty. This must be
a_rows_sample.statement: Reaffirms Zero(K,G,I)→Δ as established while flagging Δ's exact mathematical structure as unresolved, requiring experimental determination.

a_rows_sample.anchor: [ESTABLISHED] Lord(K,\Delta,G,C) \rightarrow CandidateActions ... Lord can consider both Epistemic actions (retrieve, query, inspect, measure, test, ask human) and World-changing actions (modify, deploy, migrate, approve, execute). [PROPOSED] Value of Information VOI(a) may be used to select useful
a_rows_sample.statement: Reaffirms Lord's formal signature and the epistemic/world-changing action split as established, VOI-based selection as merely proposed, and the exact action-space mathematics as unresolved.

a_rows_sample.anchor: This became one of the strongest results of the previous phase. [ESTABLISHED] Sufficiency is purpose-dependent: Sufficient(K,P,C,t). There is no useful universal predicate: Complete(K,Reality). Instead we define an EpistemicContract(P) that specifies what must be known for a particular purpose.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reaffirms purpose-relative sufficiency and the EpistemicContract as one of the strongest established results of the prior phase.

a_rows_sample.anchor: For purpose P: R(P)=\{r_1,\ldots,r_n\}. A requirement can be Satisfied, Unsatisfied, Unknown, Conflicted, NotApplicable. [PROPOSED] Weighted coverage Coverage(K,P) = \sum_i w_i Sat_i / \sum_iw_i was proposed. But Coverage\neq Readiness. Critical requirements must be evaluated separately. ... Ready(K
a_rows_sample.statement: Reaffirms the five-value requirement status enum, weighted Coverage as merely [PROPOSED] and distinct from Readiness, and the five-way Ready(K,P) conjunction with three deliberately distinct readiness levels.

a_rows_sample.anchor: [ESTABLISHED] KnowledgeOS should not pursue \max |K|. Instead MinimumSufficientKnowledge(P) is the appropriate target. This gives the system a principled stopping condition. ... [ESTABLISHED] Gap(K,P) = R(P)-Satisfied(K) conceptually identifies what remains unresolved. The gap may contain missing ev
a_rows_sample.statement: Reaffirms MinimumSufficientKnowledge(P) as the correct target (not max|K|) and the EpistemicGap Gap(K,P)=R(P)-Satisfied(K) formula, both marked established.

a_rows_sample.anchor: [ESTABLISHED] KnowledgeOS must be able to answer: Why do we know this? The conceptual structures are ProvenanceGraph, LineageGraph, CausalGraph. They are deliberately distinct: ProvenanceGraph\neq LineageGraph\neq CausalGraph. A conclusion should be traceable back to its source/evidence and derivati
a_rows_sample.statement: Reaffirms the three deliberately distinct graphs (Provenance/Lineage/Causal) as established.

a_rows_sample.anchor: [ESTABLISHED] The governance chain is Recommendation \rightarrow Decision \rightarrow Authorization \rightarrow Execution. An AI recommendation cannot directly become an execution authorization. An unknown authorization cannot be interpreted as approval. A rejected authorization must block governed
a_rows_sample.statement: Reaffirms the governance chain and its three safety properties (no AI-direct-authorization, unknown≠approval, rejection blocks execution) as established.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Step 25A is not yet a test of the whole KnowledgeOS theory. It is the first controlled experiment to see whether the minimal formal state and type system can represent the epistemic cycle without semantic contradictions. I attempted to execute the first prototype in the current environment, but the
b_rows_sample.statement: Discloses that a first prototype execution attempt did NOT successfully complete in the available environment, explicitly refusing to claim experimental results not actually obtained — proceeding instead with conceptual/formal work only, to be executed in a later tool-capable environment.

b_rows_sample.anchor: What is the smallest state required to represent KnowledgeOS without losing the distinctions established in the theory? I propose that we start with nine fundamental types, rather than implementing the much larger list.
b_rows_sample.statement: Poses the minimality question and commits to nine fundamental types rather than the much larger 21-type list proposed in the prior handover file.

b_rows_sample.anchor: WorldState W_t Represents the state of the external subject/world at time t. W_t(Nexus.version)=3.69.0. Important: W_t \neq K_t because KnowledgeOS may not know the true world state.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines WorldState W_t (worked with Nexus.version example), reaffirming W_t≠K_t.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Observation O An observation is something obtained from interacting with or observing the world. Minimal form: O=(id,subject,value,time,method,source). Observation subject = nexus.version, value = 3.69.0, time = 10:00, method = infrastructure_inventory. An observation is not yet knowledge.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Observation O=(id,subject,value,time,method,source), explicitly not yet knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence E Evidence is information that is being used to support or challenge a proposition. Minimal form: E=(id,proposition,content,origin,time,provenance). E_1: Nexus.version=3.69.0 from an infrastructure inventory. Critically: Observation\neq Evidence. An observation may become evidence, but the
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Evidence E=(id,proposition,content,origin,time,provenance), reaffirming Observation≠Evidence with the distinction required to remain visible even when an observation becomes evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Assertion A An assertion is a proposition that can be evaluated. A_1: Nexus.version=3.69.0. It has a relationship to evidence: E\rightarrow A. But A\neq Knowledge. An assertion may be candidate, supported, conflicted, committed, retracted. This is already enough to expose an important question: What
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Assertion A with a five-value status set (candidate/supported/conflicted/committed/retracted), reaffirming A≠Knowledge and explicitly leaving open what makes an assertion eligible for commitment.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Assessment Q Assessment records the epistemic evaluation of an assertion. Q(A,E,C) \rightarrow Assessment. It may eventually contain support, confidence, reliability, uncertainty, method. But we should not yet invent a probability algebra. That belongs to the later statistical work.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Assessment as Q(A,E,C)→Assessment with five candidate future fields, deliberately deferring any probability algebra to later statistical work.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeState K_t At minimum K_t = (A_t,Q_t,E_t,C_t,P_t) where assertions; assessments; relevant evidence; conflicts; provenance/lineage. This is deliberately provisional. [UNRESOLVED] Is evidence actually part of K_t, or is it external to the knowledge state and merely referenced by it? We should
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the provisional KnowledgeState K_t=(Assertions,Assessments,Evidence,Conflicts,Provenance), explicitly flagging [UNRESOLVED] whether Evidence belongs inside K_t or is merely referenced, to be settled by testing against historical reconstruction/retraction/provenance/conflict-resolution requirements, not by intuition.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Goal G A goal specifies what we want to achieve. G="Prepare Nexus for governed migration." A goal is not an action. Goal\neq Action.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Goal G, reaffirming Goal≠Action.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge Requirement R A requirement specifies what must be established for the purpose. R_1=BackupVerified, R_2=RollbackVerified, R_3=ArchitectureApproval. Then R(G)=\{R_1,R_2,R_3\}.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines KnowledgeRequirement R worked with a three-item migration requirement set R(G).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Epistemic Contract C_G The contract defines what "enough knowledge" means for this goal. C_G=\{R(G),Criticality,TemporalRequirements,AuthorityRequirements\}. Then Sufficient(K_t,C_G) becomes computable in principle. This is much stronger than asking "Does KnowledgeOS know enough?" because enough for
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines EpistemicContract C_G=(R(G),Criticality,TemporalRequirements,AuthorityRequirements), making Sufficient(K_t,C_G) computable in principle, stronger than an unqualified 'know enough?' question.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Minimal State So our first experimental state becomes: K_t=(E_t,A_t,Q_t,C_t,P_t,V_t) with G and C_G outside the knowledge state as the purpose/decision context. But I want to flag this as PROVISIONAL rather than established.
b_rows_sample.statement: Refines the minimal state to K_t=(E_t,A_t,Q_t,C_t,P_t,V_t) with Goal and EpistemicContract kept external as purpose/decision context, explicitly flagged PROVISIONAL, not established.

b_rows_sample.anchor: First state transition ... Observe(W_t) \rightarrow O then O \rightarrow E then E \rightarrow Assessment then Assessment \rightarrow Assertion then potentially Assertion \rightarrow K_{t+1}. Therefore K_{t+1} = Update(K_t,E,A,Q,C) is our first executable transition.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the first executable transition chain Observe→O→E→Assessment→Assertion→K_{t+1}, formalized as K_{t+1}=Update(K_t,E,A,Q,C).

b_rows_sample.anchor: First experiment ... K_0=\varnothing. Observation Nexus version = 3.69.0. Evidence E_1: Version(Nexus)=3.69.0. Assessment Evidence supports the assertion. Assertion A_1: Version(Nexus)=3.69.0. Commit K_1 contains the committed assertion. K_0 \xrightarrow{E_1} K_1.
b_rows_sample.statement: Walks through the smallest possible experiment from empty K_0 through a single evidence item to committed K_1.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Now we attack it ... E_2: Version(Nexus)=3.72.0. Now we have E_1\Rightarrow A_1 and E_2\Rightarrow A_2 where A_1\neq A_2. The system must produce Conflict(Version(Nexus)) rather than silently replacing 3.69.0 with 3.72.0. This is our first adversarial test.
b_rows_sample.statement: Designs the first adversarial test (a second contradicting version value) expecting an explicit Conflict marker rather than silent replacement.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Second attack — LLM ... Nexus has a verified backup. but there is no evidence supporting BackupVerified=True. Therefore LLMOutput \rightarrow CandidateAssertion but not LLMOutput \rightarrow CommittedKnowledge. Expected: Status=Unsupported or equivalent. This tests one of our strongest invariants.
b_rows_sample.statement: Designs the second adversarial test (unsupported LLM claim) expecting Status=Unsupported, testing the LLM-output/committed-knowledge boundary.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Third attack — temporal reasoning ... At t_0 we know Version=3.69. At t_1 we learn Version=3.72. The correct result is not "The old evidence was wrong." It may have been historically correct. Therefore the model needs ValidAt(E,t). This is the first indication that temporal validity is not optional.
b_rows_sample.statement: Designs the third adversarial test (successive true version changes over time), requiring ValidAt(E,t) rather than treating the older value as simply wrong — the first concrete indication that temporal validity is not optional.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Fourth attack — retraction ... E_1 is later invalidated. Retract(E_1). We cannot simply delete E_1. We must find Dependents(E_1). Then recompute affected assertions. This gives us Retraction \rightarrow DependencyAnalysis \rightarrow KnowledgeRevision.
b_rows_sample.statement: Designs the fourth adversarial test (retraction), requiring Dependents(E1) computation and recomputation of affected assertions rather than deletion.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Fifth attack — sufficiency ... K_t contains Version, Backup but not Rollback and ArchitectureApproval. Then Sufficient(K_t,C_G)=False. The important point is that we don't need universal knowledge. We only need to evaluate the explicit contract.
b_rows_sample.statement: Designs the fifth adversarial test (partial requirement satisfaction), showing Sufficient(K_t,C_G)=False evaluates only against the explicit contract, not universal knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Sixth attack — more knowledge ... The test returns Rollback=False. Previously Rollback=Unknown. Knowledge increased. But readiness remains false, and possibly becomes more decisively false. Thus the simulation should demonstrate |K_{t+1}|>|K_t| while Readiness(K_{t+1}) < Readiness(K_t) is possible.
b_rows_sample.statement: Designs the sixth adversarial test (rollback test failing), formalizing the key property |K_{t+1}|>|K_t| while Readiness(K_{t+1})<Readiness(K_t) can simultaneously hold.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'minimal-formal-state-type-system' POSSIBLY relates to 'historical-experimental-knowledge-extraction-handover' (batch B0021). Note: S0886's Step 25A.1: honestly discloses a failed prototype-execution attempt (no fabricated results); defines nine minimal fundamental types with worked examples; flags K_t's exact composition (esp. whether Evidence is inside or merely referenced) as explicitly UNRESOLVED, to be tested rather than assumed; walks a minimal experiment plus seven adversarial attacks; lists eight pressure points and a 15-row status assessment; concludes Zero/Lord/Sarathi must wait for KnowledgeState finalization; hands off to Step 25A.2 (executable Evidence->Assessment->Assertion experiment).

a_rows_sample.anchor: The Ideal State is the Knower's current model of what the Knowledge State should be ... I_t = (D_I, V_I, R_I, Sigma_I, C_I, P_I) ... Ideal State \neq Knowledge State ... Ideal State \neq Truth
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Ideal State as the Knower's model of desired dimensions/values/relationships/epistemic-state/constraints/purpose, explicitly distinct from both the current Knowledge State and Truth, and shown to be dynamic (I_{t+1}=Revision(I_t,K_t,U_t)) and both purpose-dependent (I_t(P)!=I_t(P')) and Knower-dependent (I_t(N)!=I_t(N')).

a_rows_sample.anchor: I^K_t \neq I^U_t \neq I^D_t ... I^K: what should be known ... I^U: how the knowledge should be understood/held ... I^D: what the domain reality should become
a_rows_sample.statement: Splits the single Ideal State into three distinguishable forms -- Ideal Knowledge State I^K (what should be known), Ideal Understanding State I^U (how knowledge should be understood/interpreted/applied for decision purposes), and Ideal Domain State I^D (what domain reality should become) -- resolving an ambiguity where 'ideal' had conflated epistemic target with normative/domain target.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Arjuna could possess facts such as Bhishma=grandfather without yet understanding what those facts mean for his decision. Knowledge \neq Understanding.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues via the Arjuna case that Knowledge != Understanding: possessing a fact does not entail grasping its decision-relevant implications, motivating the separate Ideal Understanding State I^U and the corresponding Understanding-comparison operation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I^D_t \Rightarrow Requirements(I^K_t) ... I^K_t \Rightarrow Requirements(I^U_t) ... these are requirements/derivations, not identities. We must not write I^D=I^K or I^K=I^U.
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes that the three Ideal forms are not independent (a desired domain state generates knowledge requirements, which generate understanding requirements) but must never be treated as identical, preventing collapse of domain/knowledge/understanding targets into one object.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K uparrow and Certainty downarrow ... Q_{t+1} \neq Q_t. The Knower discovers that the original question was inadequate.
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates via the Arjuna case that increased knowledge can accompany decreased certainty because the ideal knowledge target I^K itself grows (I^K_0 -> I^K_1) once new dimensions are discovered, sometimes producing a revised question Q_{t+1} != Q_t rather than a direct answer to Q_t.

a_rows_sample.anchor: D_E(K_t,I^K_t) \rightarrow 0 \not\Rightarrow Journey Complete ... I^K_2 \neq I^K_0 ... Knowledge acquisition can move the Ideal State. KnowledgeOS is not solving a static optimization problem. It is solving a dynamic epistemic navigation problem.
a_rows_sample.statement: Shows via the Arjuna example that measured distance reaching zero (D_E(K_2,I^K_0)=0) does not mean the epistemic journey is complete, because the Ideal State itself evolved in step (I^K_2 != I^K_0); reframes KnowledgeOS's problem as dynamic epistemic navigation rather than static optimization against a fixed target.

a_rows_sample.anchor: If the Ideal State is allowed to adapt freely to the Current Knowledge State, the system can make its own epistemic deficit disappear ... Current Knowledge must not silently redefine its own target ... Declared Ideal / Derived Ideal / Exploratory Horizon
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies a critical safety failure mode: since the Ideal State is defined as dynamically revisable (I_{t+1}=Revision(I_t,K_t,...)), nothing prevents it from being set equal to current knowledge (I_t:=K_t), silently erasing all epistemic deficit even though the Knower remains ignorant; introduces the invariant 'current knowledge must not silently redefine its own target' and splits Ideal State into Declared Ideal (what the Knower explicitly requires), Derived Ideal (what KnowledgeOS derives from purpose/context/domain), and Exploratory Horizon (what Lord proposes might matter) to prevent this collapse.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Do not use 'all understanding' as an Ideal State; use purpose-relative sufficiency ... I^U(P) = Decision-relevant understanding sufficient for P, not I^U = Complete understanding. Adequacy \neq Completeness.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the Ideal Understanding State from an impossible 'all implications understood' target to a purpose-relative sufficiency criterion (decision-relevant implications identified and sufficiently understood for the given purpose P), consistent with the earlier Adequacy != Completeness distinction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I_{t+1} = Revision(I_t, K_t, U_t, X_t, N_t) ... The Knower is the ultimate authority over the Ideal State. KnowledgeOS != I_t; KnowledgeOS -> Suggestions for I_t; Knower -> I_t.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Ideal State evolution as a deterministic Revision function of prior ideal, current knowledge/understanding/domain state and the Knower, with six sources of change (knowledge-driven, understanding-driven, domain-driven, purpose-driven, context-driven, Knower-driven), most modelled as monotonic union-additions to the ideal, and states the Knower as sole ultimate authority over I_t.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knower Intent != Ideal State Authority... The Knower cannot simply redefine a mandatory regulatory requirement... IdealState = KnowerIntent + ApplicableNorms + Constraints + Purpose, not simply IdealState=KnowerPreference.
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the absolute claim that the Knower alone owns/controls the Ideal State: real Ideal States are also constrained by law, organizational policy, domain rules, contractual obligations, safety constraints, architecture governance and regulatory requirements the Knower cannot unilaterally override -- IdealState is composed of KnowerIntent plus ApplicableNorms plus Constraints plus Purpose, never reducible to KnowerPreference alone.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I strongly recommend introducing: I-hat_t = Candidate Ideal State and I_t = Approved Ideal State ... KnowledgeOS -> I-hat_{t+1} (proposal); Authorize(I-hat_{t+1}) -> I_{t+1}.
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces a Candidate Ideal State (I-hat) vs Approved Ideal State (I) split mirroring the Q17 recommendation/authorization boundary: KnowledgeOS may only ever produce a candidate revision proposal, and only an explicit Authorize step (by the Knower/governance authority under applicable norms) produces the actually approved I_{t+1}; KnowledgeOS != I_{t+1} but KnowledgeOS -> I-hat_{t+1}.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Given the same inputs, there is one correct Ideal State. That is not true... several legitimate responses: increase security requirement; change the purpose; accept the risk; change the architecture; defer the decision. RevisionCandidates: S_t -> P(I).
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects modelling Ideal-State Revision as a deterministic function returning one correct new ideal, since the same discovered deficiency (e.g. insufficient security) admits multiple legitimate responses (strengthen requirement, change purpose, accept risk, change architecture, defer); replaces it with RevisionCandidates producing a power-set of possible ideal states, from which Authorize selects the approved one.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the union equations are too strong ... this assumes Ideal State evolution is monotonic expansion.
